Short: Add checksum verification for included remote config files.
Short: Add config option to set default API base URL (api.baseUrl).

MEDIUM: The CLI currently ignores environment variables that contain dots (e.g. DB.HOST). We need to enhance env var parsing so that underscores map to nested keys (DB_HOST -> db.host) and support a configurable map. This helps in containerized deployments where only flat env vars are available.

MEDIUM: In CI, our teams want to centrally manage config but allow repo-level overrides. Add support for a global /etc/cli/config.yaml that loads before project .cli-config.yaml, with clear precedence rules and an option to disable global loading per repo.

MEDIUM: The config merging algorithm currently does a shallow merge, which causes arrays to be replaced instead of merged. Change merge behavior to deep-merge objects and concatenate arrays with deduplication for plugin lists.

MEDIUM: We need per-environment config sections (development, staging, production). Add an --env flag that picks the appropriate section and also supports fallback inheritance (production inherits from default).

MEDIUM: When users supply invalid enum values in config, the CLI crashes with a stack trace. Add schema-based validation and map invalid values to suggestions using levenstein distance (e.g. 'debbug' -> 'debug').
MEDIUM: Add a config option to enable a proxy for outbound HTTP calls (http.proxy). Ensure the HTTP client respects NO_PROXY patterns from config and env vars.
MEDIUM: Our config loader is synchronous and blocks startup. Make loading async to allow remote config fetching, and display a spinner for interactive use while fetching remote pieces.
MEDIUM: Add an audit trail feature—store the last N config changes (with timestamp and actor if available) in ~/.config/cli/config_history.json and surface them via --config-history.
MEDIUM: Allow users to specify a secrets provider in config (secrets.provider = 'vault' | 'aws' | 'file') and resolve secret placeholders at runtime before use.
MEDIUM: The init command should generate comments and examples in the generated config file tailored to detected environment (e.g. if Node.js project detected, show node-specific examples).
MEDIUM: Add configuration for plugin discovery path (plugins.paths) so enterprise users can install company-provided plugins outside node_modules.
MEDIUM: Provide a --dry-run that shows what config would be applied (merges and resolved secrets) without making network calls or writing files.
MEDIUM: Add config-driven rate limiting (http.rateLimit = {requests: 100, perSeconds: 60}) and ensure the CLI honors it for API calls made by commands.
MEDIUM: Support JSON5 config files so users can leave trailing commas and comments. Validate and fallback to JSON/YAML if parse fails.
MEDIUM: Provide a 'config lint' command that checks for deprecated keys and prints migration guidance when old keys are detected.
MEDIUM: For monorepos, add support for workspace-scoped configs (workspaces/*/.cli-config.yaml) and a root-level aggregator that merges them for multi-package runs.
MEDIUM: Add the ability to encrypt parts of the config with a master key stored in OS keychain; the CLI should decrypt on load and re-encrypt on save.
MEDIUM: Add a default-config preset system: users can select presets (e.g. 'fast-build', 'ci-optimized') via config.presets and the CLI applies preset overrides on load.

LONG: When loading config files we get a parse error for some users. Example stack trace:

Error: YAMLException: bad indentation of a mapping entry at line 12, column 3:
    plugins:
      - name: foo
      ^
    at Object.generateError (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/cli/node_modules/js-yaml/lib/js-yaml/loader.js:162:10)
    at throwError (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/cli/node_modules/js-yaml/lib/js-yaml/loader.js:168:9)
    at readBlockMapping (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/cli/node_modules/js-yaml/lib/js-yaml/loader.js:1066:7)

This happens when users paste config snippets that include tab indentation. Update our config loader to normalize tabs -> spaces before parsing and show a clearer message pointing to the offending line. Also include a code snippet to auto-fix common indentation problems.

Suggested code:

const fs = require('fs');
let raw = fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
raw = raw.replace(/\t/g, '  ');
const config = yaml.load(raw);

LONG: Config merging bug when using plugins. Reproduction:
1) global config (~/.config/cli/config.yaml):
plugins:
  - name: 'a'
  - name: 'b'
2) project .cli-config.yaml:
plugins:
  - name: 'b'
  - name: 'c'

Expected merged plugins: a,b,c (deduplicated). Actual result: project plugins replaced global plugins => b,c.

Stack trace when running 'cli --debug':
TypeError: cfg.plugins.map is not a function
    at Object.normalizePlugins (/usr/local/lib/cli/lib/plugins.js:18:12)

Proposed change: deep-merge arrays by concatenation with dedup on 'name' property. Sample implementation:

function mergePlugins(globalPlugins = [], projectPlugins = []) {
  const map = new Map();
  [...globalPlugins, ...projectPlugins].forEach(p => map.set(p.name, p));
  return Array.from(map.values());
}

LONG: We need environment interpolation and fallback logic. Problem: When config contains ${DB_URL} and DB_URL isn't set, the CLI throws ReferenceError. Repro:

$ cat .cli-config.yaml
database:
  url: "${DB_URL}"

$ node bin/cli.js start

Error: DB_URL is not defined
    at interpolate (/usr/local/lib/cli/lib/config.js:55:13)

Proposed: implement safe interpolation with optional defaults like ${DB_URL:postgres://localhost:5432/default}. Example implementation:

function interpolate(str, env) {
  return str.replace(/\$\{([^:}]+)(:([^}]+))?\}/g, (_, key, __, def) => env[key] || def || '');
}

LONG: Logging improvement for config errors. Current behavior on invalid config:

Error: Invalid config
    at Object.loadConfig (/usr/local/lib/cli/lib/config.js:10:15)

This lacks context. Proposed changes:
- Include file path, line and column when available
- Print snippet around the error (3 lines before/after)
- Provide actionable suggestions (e.g., 'Did you forget a comma?')

Example output:
Error parsing ~/.config/cli/config.yaml: unexpected character at line 12, column 5
10 |   plugins:
11 |     - name: foo
12 |     - name: bar	\t<-- unexpected tab
13 |     - name: baz

Action: replace tabs with 2 spaces or run 'cli config fix'.

Implement by catching parser errors and using error.mark from js-yaml, then reading file and printing surrounding lines.

LONG: Support for multiple profiles in config. Use-case: devs want multiple credential profiles (staging, prod) and switch with --profile flag. Proposed config structure:

profiles:
  staging:
    apiKey: 'stg-...'
    api.baseUrl: 'https://stg.api'
  production:
    apiKey: 'prod-...'

Implement --profile lookup, fallback to default profile, and avoid leaking secrets when printing config. Provide CLI behavior examples and ensure profile selection affects all subcommands and plugin loaders. Example code:

function selectProfile(cfg, name){
  return merge(cfg.default || {}, cfg.profiles?.[name] || {});
}

LONG: Add a 'config apply' subcommand that writes the effective config to a chosen location (stdout, file, or remote store). Requirements:
- Should accept --format json|yaml
- Should redact secrets by default, with --show-secrets to reveal
- Should preserve comments when writing YAML if possible

Use case: CI needs to capture merged config and push it to a remote artifact. Include sample usage and example output. Example implementation approach using js-yaml and a redact function:

function redact(cfg){ /* deep clone and replace secret fields with '<redacted>' */ }

LONG: Add support for JSON pointer based overrides via CLI: --set /api/timeout=3000 to set nested values without writing a full config. Specs:
- Accept multiple --set flags
- Validate pointers against schema
- Apply and optionally write back to a specified file with --write-config

Example CLI usage: cli --set /api/timeout=3000 --set /plugins/0/enabled=false --write-config ./cli-config.yaml

Implementation hint: use jsonpointer npm module and convert string values to typed values with a heuristic parser (numbers, booleans, null). Provide example function to parse value:

function parseValue(str){ if (str === 'null') return null; if (/^\d+$/.test(str)) return Number(str); if (/^(true|false)$/i.test(str)) return str.toLowerCase()==='true'; return str; }
Normalize SDK error codes to a single enum and export it from the root package so consumers can reliably switch on error types.
Throw typed errors (class ApiError extends Error) instead of plain Error across HTTP client so callers can instanceof-check.
Wrap network requests with a configurable retry/backoff strategy for transient 5xx and network failures.
Add an option to enable/disable automatic error telemetry so users can opt out of sending error reports.
Ensure SDK does not swallow errors in Promise chains; rethrow or reject instead of console.error only.
Make all public async functions return Promise<Result<T, SDKError>> union type instead of throwing for better TS ergonomics.
Replace any use of 'any' in error handling code with a discriminated union for known error shapes.
Add source-map-supported stack traces when bundling the SDK for browser consumers so errors map to TS sources.
Fix unhandled rejection in WebSocket reconnection flow when server sends malformed JSON.
Expose a hook (onError) that consumers can register to transform or annotate errors before they're logged.
Add structured logging context (requestId, userId, correlationId) to every error emitted from the SDK.
Prevent infinite error loops: when onError or telemetry call throws, catch and avoid re-emitting the same error.
Document SDK error types and codes in README, including sample switch statements for handling transient vs permanent errors.
Return 4xx responses as SDKClientError with status and body parsed into typed interface, not generic Error.
Make the default HTTP client timeout configurable and surface TimeoutError with original request details.
Fix bug where GraphQL errors get lost: include graphQLErrors array on the thrown error object when response contains errors.
Add test coverage for network failures using msw that asserts correct error shapes are returned to consumers.
Add consistent error.name for all custom errors (e.g., 'SDKApiError', 'SDKTimeoutError') so instanceof and name checks both work.
Ensure SDK errors preserve original stack traces when wrapped; set error.stack = original.stack + '\nCaused by: ...'.
Improve TypeScript type definitions: exported error classes should implement an interface ISDKError { code: string; status?: number }.
Refactor fetch wrapper to throw SDKNetworkError on non-2xx with response.json parsed safely and fallback to text.
The SDK currently swallows JSON.parse errors when reading response bodies. We need to surface a DeserializationError with raw body for debugging.
When token refresh fails, SDK should emit an AuthenticationError and halt retries. Right now it keeps retrying forever.
Add an option to attach original request payload to errors for internal debugging, gated behind a debug flag to avoid PII leaks.
Change the retry logic to respect Retry-After header when rate-limited (429) and use exponential backoff otherwise.
Fix race condition in concurrency limiter that causes 'QueueOverflowError' to be thrown sporadically under heavy load.
Handle circular references in error serialization for telemetry by using a safe serializer (e.g., JSON-safe-stringify).
Make sure database errors (e.g., UNIQUE constraint) are translated to user-friendly SDK errors with code 'ConflictError'.
Add Client-Side validation errors (ValidationError) with field-level messages instead of returning HTTP 400 raw bodies.
Ensure server-side stack traces are not leaked in production builds; include full stack only when sdk.debug = true.
Update examples to show how to use try/catch with async SDK methods and how to inspect error.code and error.details.
Short: Create SDKError union type and export it from index.ts.
Short: Throw SDKTimeoutError when request times out instead of generic Error.
Short: Add onError hook to the client constructor.
Short: Replace console.error with logger.error that can be swapped by consumer.
Short: Add proper typings for GraphQL error responses in SDK types.
Short: Fail fast on invalid API key and return AuthenticationError synchronously.
Short: Preserve stack traces when wrapping errors in custom classes.
Short: Add retry-on-idempotent setting for unsafe methods to be disabled by default.
Short: Expose error codes as const enum in types file.
Short: Sanitize user input before including it in error messages to avoid XSS.
Short: Add a test that ensures unhandledRejection is not triggered by SDK internals.
Short: Return parsed error body under error.payload property.
Short: Add capability to map HTTP status codes to SDK error classes via config.
Short: Emit deprecation warnings as specific DeprecationWarning error type.
Short: Make parseError safe for empty response bodies ('' → null payload).
Short: Support a callback to filter which errors get sent to telemetry.

Medium: The SDK's fetch layer sometimes returns an Error with no status or body when a server responds with empty 204 and JSON parsing is attempted. We should detect empty bodies and return a clear NoContentError or null payload instead of throwing a SyntaxError on JSON.parse.

Medium: When using the SDK in React apps, unhandled exceptions inside error boundary callbacks originated from the SDK are not preserved. We should ensure thrown SDK errors are instances of Error with meaningful message and name so React error boundaries can pick them up and display consistent error UIs.

Medium: Our GraphQL client currently discards operation.context and queryName when wrapping errors. Add preservation of operation metadata and attach queryName and variables (sanitized) to the error object for easier debugging.

Medium: We need better documentation and code examples for mapping HTTP 401 -> AuthenticationError and automatically attempting token refresh once. Include a sample middleware showing how to plug into the SDK's request pipeline.

Medium: Add graceful degradation for binary responses: if response headers indicate no JSON (Content-Type missing or not application/json), do not attempt to parse and set error.rawBody to ArrayBuffer or text depending on content-type.

Medium: Sometimes the SDK logs 'Uncaught (in promise) undefined' in browsers when network fails. Track down where rejections are resolved without passing the error through, and ensure all Promise rejects pass a consistent Error subclass with message and code.
Medium: Add an option 'suppressWarnings' that disables non-fatal console.warn logs from SDK internals. Right now those warnings also get forwarded to our telemetry unfilted which pollutes dashboards.

Medium: The TypeScript definitions for error handlers and middleware are too permissive (allow any). Tighten types to (err: SDKError) => Promise<void> | void and provide examples for augmenting errors with requestId.

Medium: On server-side Node usage, a large JSON error response causes heap growth when we attach the entire response to the Error. Provide a safe truncation policy (configurable) and tests that verify big responses are truncated in error.payload.

Medium: When the SDK receives a 401, it attempts refresh and retries once, but if refresh fails it throws a generic Error. Change this to throw AuthenticationError with a reason code 'REFRESH_FAILED' and include refresh response body for debugging.
Medium: Add clear migration notes for users upgrading to new error model: previously errors were strings; now they're classes. Provide codemods or examples for migrating try/catch blocks.

Medium: In the browser bundle we accidentally polyfilled Error.prepareStackTrace causing weird stack traces. Remove that polyfill and ensure node/browser stacks remain readable and mapped to source maps when available.
Medium: Add a diagnostic command (client.diagnoseError(err)) that returns normalized metadata (type, code, status, requestUrl, requestId) useful for CLI debugging and tests.
Medium: The SDK's retry mechanism doesn't surface the number of attempts in the error. Add error.attempts field and include lastResponse and lastError for troubleshooting.
Medium: Ensure that when user-provided onError handler throws, SDK logs the handler error separately but preserves and rethrows the original SDK error to the consumer.
Medium: Update error serialization for telemetry to include module version, environment, and whether the error is retriable. Add tests to assert telemetry payload shape.

Medium: Fix a bug where aborting a fetch via AbortController results in a generic Error('Aborted') that lacks the AbortError name. Create and throw an SDKAbortError with reason and original signal info.

Long: Crash on production when response.json() throws because body is HTML. Repro steps and stack:

Reproduction:
1) Call client.get('/users/123')
2) Server returns 500 with HTML error page (Content-Type: text/html)
3) SDK attempts response.json() and throws SyntaxError

Stack trace:
SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at Response.json (node_modules/node-fetch/lib/index.js:xxx:yy)
    at parseResponse (/src/http.ts:48:15)
    at handleResponse (/src/http.ts:78:10)

Suggested fix: detect Content-Type header and if not application/json, set error.rawBody = await response.text() and throw DeserializationError with rawBody and status. Also add unit test using msw to return HTML 500 and assert error.rawBody contains '<!DOCTYPE'.

Long: Intermittent unhandledRejection in WebSocket reconnect logic. Example code and logs below.

Client code:

const ws = sdk.createRealtimeClient({ url: 'wss://realtime.example.com' });
ws.on('message', handler);

Logs:
UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError: Cannot read property 'emit' of undefined
    at ReconnectHandler (/dist/realtime.js:200:22)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)

Issue: When reconnection occurs, internal state 'this.socket' sometimes becomes null and we attempt to emit error on closed emitter. Need strong null checks and ensure reconnection queue awaits previous cleanup. Add tests that simulate abrupt close and restore to reproduce.

Suggested change: wrap all emitter calls with if (this.emitter) and ensure async cleanup await this._cleanupPromise before reconnecting.

Long: Fatal leak: errors include huge circular request objects causing telemetry to fail JSON.stringify. Example error payload and stack:

Error: Failed to serialize error for telemetry
    at TelemetryClient.send (/dist/telemetry.js:72:18)

Sample thrown error:
{
  name: 'SDKApiError',
  message: 'Request failed',
  request: { url: '/heavy', body: { a: 1, parent: [Circular] } }
}

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create a request with object referencing itself
const obj: any = {}; obj.self = obj;
2) client.post('/heavy', obj)

Fix: Implement a safe serializer in telemetry (like cycle-safe replacer) and add redact/whitelist options for fields. Also ensure error.toJSON only serializes safe fields (name, message, code, status, truncated payload). Add unit tests covering circular structures and large payload truncation.

Long: Production bug: SDK swallows database errors when used in serverless functions. Logs show 'Handled error but returning 200'. Example trace and reproduction steps.

Reproduction in AWS Lambda:
1) initialize client inside handler
2) call client.createRecord(payload) which triggers DB unique violation

Observed outcome: Lambda returns 200 and response body contains { ok: true } though DB operation failed. Logs show:
[info] Operation failed, handled silently

Root cause: error middleware calls next() without rethrowing or passing the error to the final handler. Middleware signature misused. The middleware should call next(err) or throw. Fix middleware pipeline to ensure if a middleware handles error and wants to swallow it it must set response explicitly; otherwise propagate. Add tests for serverless integration where unhandled errors propagate and return 500.

Suggestion: change internal pipeline to treat missing next(err) and missing response as a bug and throw an UnhandledMiddlewareError with stack pointing to middleware origin.

Long: The SDK's error messages expose internal SQL queries in production Sentry reports. Example captured message:

Error: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_email_key" at INSERT INTO users (email, name) VALUES ...

Security issue: these messages may contain PII or internal structure. Need to redact queries and PII by default in telemetry. Proposed approach:
- Add telemetry.sanitize = true by default
- Error.toTelemetry() returns redacted message and meta: { constraint: 'users_email_key' }
- Provide allowlist config for fields to include

Implementation details: use regex to replace INSERT/UPDATE statements and email patterns, but also allow plugin hooks so teams can implement custom redaction. Add examples and tests verifying query strings are replaced with '<REDACTED_SQL>'.

Long: SDK's metrics and error counters miscount because thrown error is replaced by a new Error before metrics increment. Example timeline:

1) request fails with DBError
2) we wrap into ApiError and throw
3) metrics.inc('errors', { type: ApiError }) called, but code path increments based on original error code elsewhere so counts mismatch

Fix: centralize error classification before wrapping. Implement classifyError(original) => { code, retriable, category } then increment metrics using classification result, and finally throw wrapped error that includes classification. Provide unit tests and example classification function. Also update types so classifyError returns a stable enum to avoid string mismatches.

Long: Bulk operations return mixed successes and failures, but SDK currently fails the whole batch on first error. Requirements and proposal:

Requirement: For batch endpoints, return BatchResult<T> = { successes: T[]; failures: Array<{ index: number; error: ISDKError }>; } rather than throwing when any item fails.

Current usage:
await client.bulkInsert(items); // throws on first failure

Requested change: add client.bulkInsert(items, { partial: true }) option. When partial true, SDK should parse response and return BatchResult. Provide TypeScript types and example:

type BulkInsertOptions = { partial?: boolean };
async function bulkInsert<T>(items: T[], opts?: BulkInsertOptions): Promise<void | BatchResult<T>>;

Add tests where server returns 207 Multi-Status with per-item results and assert SDK returns BatchResult with typed failures and no throw. Update docs and migration notes.

Long: Unexpected TLS error on Node 12 during HTTPS request causing generic 'socket hang up'. Stack trace and suggested debugging:

Error: socket hang up
    at connResetException (internal/errors.js:560:14)
    at TLSSocket.socketOnEnd (_http_client.js:455:23)
    at TLSSocket.emit (events.js:198:13)

We should capture underlying TLS errors and wrap them in SDKNetworkError with code 'TLS_ERROR' and include cipher and protocol if available from socket.getCipher() and socket.getProtocol(). Also validate that the SDK supports minimum Node versions and document required Node TLS config. Add a low-level hook to allow consumers to inspect underlying Node socket info on network errors.

Implementation: inside http/agent.ts attach 'secureConnect' and on 'error' read socket.getCipher() and socket.getProtocol() and include them in error.meta. Add tests using nock to simulate socket hang-up and assert meta has e.g. { protocol: 'TLSv1.2' }.
Remove unused serde_json import in src/api/mod.rs and run cargo fmt; it's causing a clippy warning in CI.
Replace unwrap() calls in request handlers with proper error handling returning ApiError so we don't panic on malformed JSON.
Refactor duplicated pagination logic in users and posts endpoints into a shared util function.
Rename ambiguous route /get to /status and update docs to reflect API semantics.
Remove dead code for legacy OAuth1 support (auth/oauth1.rs) and corresponding feature flag.
Fix lint: change Vec::new() then push in build_response to a vec![] literal for clarity.
Update README examples to use serde_json::json! macro instead of manual Value construction.
Consolidate two DB pool initializers into a single function and ensure it uses the same sqlx::PgPoolOptions config.
Replace manual thread::spawn in background jobs with tokio::spawn for async compatibility.
Simplify match arms in auth middleware: use if let Some(user) = ... pattern to reduce nesting.
Move constant API_VERSION into crate::config and remove multiple copies across modules.
Switch clap 2 -> clap 4 usage in bin/cli.rs; clean up deprecated API usage and flags.
Remove trailing whitespace and fix indent in src/api/errors.rs to satisfy rustfmt.
Unify error types: convert crate::errors::DbError variants into a single anyhow::Error with context.
Shorten log messages to avoid exceeding stdout width in Docker logs.
The admin frontend is pulling a typed response as String. Update API to return JSON object with explicit schema.
Optimize JSON encoding by deriving Serialize on DTOs rather than serializing a HashMap each time.
Replace manual timestamp formatting with chrono::serde feature to ensure consistent timezone handling.
Remove unused feature flag 'legacy-auth' and clean up cfg attributes across the codebase.
Refactor session cookie builder to set SameSite=Lax for API endpoints instead of default None.

Medium: In src/routes/user.rs the update_user handler uses nested match and lots of cloning. Please refactor to use early returns and borrow data where possible to reduce clones. This will reduce memory churn during high load.

Medium: The OpenAPI schema generation step currently includes internal-only endpoints. Add a #[doc(hidden)] or a config option to exclude admin routes and regenerate api_spec.json. Also update CI to fail if api_spec.json is stale.
Medium: Our healthcheck endpoint returns 200 even when DB is down. Add a DB ping and return 503 if unreachable. Also add a short unit test that mocks the sqlx::PgPool to simulate a failing ping.

Medium: Tests are flaky because they share a global Tokio runtime. Migrate tests to use #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)] and remove the manual runtime creation in tests/common/mod.rs.
Medium: There are several places using Box<dyn Error> in public APIs. Replace with thiserror to produce typed errors (ApiError) that implement Display and appropriate status codes.
Medium: We still use actix_web::HttpResponse::Ok().json(...) in many places. Introduce a helper respond_json<T: Serialize>(status, body) to standardize JSON headers and tracing for requests.
Medium: The database migrations folder contains both SQL and .bak files. Remove backups and ensure migration scripts are idempotent; update migration_guide.md with the correct steps.
Medium: In src/auth/jwt.rs, token expiry is hardcoded to 24h. Make it configurable via Config.jwt_expiry_secs and update tests to use smaller durations for faster runs.
Medium: Replace manual Base64 decoding with base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD, and add error mapping to ApiError::InvalidInput for consistent 400 responses.
Medium: The logging setup uses env_logger with default RUST_LOG. Move init to crate::logging::init and ensure we set log timestamps and JSON output in production.
Medium: Remove serde(flatten) usage in service payloads — it hides schema and causes generated OpenAPI to be incorrect. Restructure types to be explicit.
Medium: Consolidate rate limiter logic into middleware rather than duplicating in each route handler. Use governor crate and add integration test to simulate bursts.
Medium: In web UI integration, change the fetch call to include credentials: 'include' and update server CORS policy to allow credentials from our frontend origin.
Medium: Clean up SQLx query strings to use query_as! where possible to get compile-time checked SQL; start with src/repos/user_repo.rs and fix compile issues.

Long: We're getting occasional panics in production with this backtrace. Need a code cleanup and safer error handling around DB access.

Stack trace (partial):
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'called Option::unwrap() on a None value', src/repos/user_repo.rs:112:21
stack backtrace:
   0: rust_begin_unwind
   1: core::panicking::panic_fmt
   2: core::option::expect_none
   3: crate::repos::user_repo::get_user_by_email
   4: crate::handlers::auth::login

Repro steps: sometimes when a user signs in with a social provider, email is missing and unwrap() causes panic. Replace unwraps in get_user_by_email with Result<Option<User>, DbError> and propagate ApiError::Unauthorized when user not found. Add unit tests showing Option::None path.

Example problematic code:

fn get_user_by_email(pool: &PgPool, email: &str) -> User {
    sqlx::query_as!(User, "SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE email = $1", email)
        .fetch_one(pool)
        .await
        .unwrap()
}

Suggested cleanup: return Result<Option<User>, sqlx::Error> and use fetch_optional().

Long: DB connection leaks: logs show 'max connections exceeded' after a spike in traffic. Investigate code paths that open PgPool connections per-request.

Sample log:
WARN sqlx::postgres::connection: connection error: error: remaining connection slots are reserved

We have several functions that take pool: PgPool rather than &PgPool and call pool.acquire().await repeatedly. Audit repository functions and change signatures to accept &PgPool (or Arc<PgPool> stored in AppState) and ensure acquire is awaited and connections are returned promptly. Example patterns to fix:

pub async fn list_users(pool: PgPool) -> Result<Vec<User>, DbError> { ... }

Change to:

pub async fn list_users(pool: &PgPool) -> Result<Vec<User>, DbError> { ... }

Also check background tasks that may spawn without limits and hold connections. Add monitoring metrics in code to count active connections using PgPool::size() if available.

Long: Flaky test failure in integration tests: 'test_create_and_fetch_item' times out randomly. Reproduction steps:

1) Run cargo test --test integration_tests -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
2) Observe occasional timeouts in create flow on CI with timeout waiting for DB migration lock.

Logs:
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'deadline elapsed', src/main.rs:200:10
Caused by: Deadline elapsed

Root cause appears to be synchronous migration lock and test parallelism. Code shows blocking::unblock calls and blocking file I/O during migrations. Clean up by making migrations async via sqlx::migrate::Migrator and ensure the test harness uses a per-test transient DB (create random schema names or use dockerized ephemeral DB). Also reduce migration set or pre-bake an image for CI to prevent lock contention.

Add instructions in CONTRIBUTING.md for running integration tests locally using docker-compose.

Long: Concurrency issue with shared cache using Arc<Mutex<HashMap>> causing lock contention. Replace with tokio::sync::RwLock or DashMap. Example problematic pattern in src/cache.rs:

async fn get(key: &str) -> Option<Value> {
    let mut guard = CACHE.lock().await; // blocks concurrent reads
    guard.get(key).cloned()
}

Recommended change:
- Use DashMap for high contention paths
- For read-mostly, use RwLock and acquire read lock when reading

Refactor code, run load tests simulating 500 concurrent requests to verify latency improvement. Document changes in ARCHITECTURE.md.

Long: There's a mismatch between API docs and actual server behavior for PATCH /users/{id}. Docs list optional fields in the body, but implementation uses serde(flatten) which makes it accept arbitrary keys and ignore validation. Reproduce:

Request: PATCH /users/123 { "unknown": "value" }
Server: returns 200 with no changes

Fix: Define explicit UpdateUser struct with Option<T> for each allowed field and remove flatten. Add validation at service layer for email format and username length. Update OpenAPI spec and regenerate client. Add tests for unknown fields causing 400.

Long: Inconsistent character encoding: frontend sends UTF-8 emoji in JSON and server records as � bytes in DB. Logs show error when inserting into text column: 'invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x00'. Found code that truncates strings via .as_bytes().to_vec() and stores raw bytes with NULs. Example code:

let s = input.trim_end_matches('\0');
db_insert(s.as_bytes())

Please sanitize inputs to remove control characters and use String directly; validate with s.is_char_boundary and remove internal NULs. Add DB constraint tests and input sanitization in request deserializers. Also add a middleware to reject payloads containing NUL with 400.

Long: Please remove feature-gated codepaths for 'unstable-api' that are no longer used. Search for cfg(feature = "unstable-api") and delete code and tests. Example leftover in src/api/legacy.rs contains deprecated endpoints that conflict with new routes and generate duplicate OpenAPI entries. After removal, run cargo test and cargo doc to ensure nothing else references these items. Update changelog to mention the removal of unstable feature flag.

Long: API input validation inconsistent: some deserializers use serde(validating) crate, others use manual checks. Consolidate by creating validators in crate::validation and using validator crate with derive macros. Example: current email validation in two places uses regex and differ. Replace with:

#[derive(Deserialize, Validate)]
struct CreateUser { #[validate(email)] email: String, ... }

Wire validation errors into ApiError::Validation with fields map. Update unit tests to reflect unified errors and remove duplicated regex modules. Also add benchmark for validation performance.

Long: Remove outdated database index creation code in src/db/migrations that duplicates an index with a different name causing Postgres to warn on migration apply. Log:

NOTICE: index "idx_users_email" already exists, skipping

Fix migration SQL to use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS where appropriate, or check prior migrations. Ensure production migrations are idempotent and safe for large tables. Provide a script to detect duplicate index definitions across migrations and run locally before deploying.

Long: Several modules still use async-std futures in examples and tests while project standard is tokio. For consistency and to avoid feature bloat, convert tests and examples to tokio runtime. Specific files: examples/client.rs and tests/load_test.rs. Example change in tests/load_test.rs:

#[async_std::test]
async fn heavy_load() { ... }

Change to:

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn heavy_load() { ... }

Update Cargo.toml to remove async-std dependency unless needed by third-party crates. Run cargo test to update snapshots if any.

Long: Logging exposes sensitive info: stack traces in error logs include API keys. Example log:

ERROR: failed to store webhook: ApiKey("sk_test_..."), backtrace: ...

Audit error Display/Debug implementations across crate to ensure secrets are redacted. Implement a Redacted type with Display masking and implement Debug to hide. Replace usage of ApiKey(String) Debug printing. Add unit tests ensuring secrets are not present in logs and verify grep across repo for '.unwrap()' on ApiKey or format!("{:?}", key) usage.

Long: Remove serde(default) on DTOs where fields are required. This hides missing field bugs. For instance UpdateProfile used #[serde(default)] causing missing fields to be defaulted rather than validated. Change to explicit Option<T> fields and validate in service layer. Add breaking-change note in CHANGELOG and adapt client tests accordingly.

Also ensure that when migrating, feature flag for compatibility remains for one release cycle before removal.

Long: Cleanup: unify HTTP client usage across the codebase. Currently some modules use reqwest blocking, wasm-bindgen-futures, and hyper clients. Standardize on reqwest::Client with a wrapper crate::http::HttpClient that supports retries, timeouts, and tracing. Replace instances in src/integrations/* to use the wrapper and remove hyper and blocking dependencies from Cargo.toml. Add unit tests mocking external HTTP via httpmock crate.

Long: The GraphQL endpoint is brittle because it accepts unknown enum variants and panics in match arms. Example stack:

thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'non-exhaustive match', src/graphql/schema.rs:345:17

Code:

match input.level.as_str() {
  "INFO" => Level::Info,
  "ERROR" => Level::Error,
}

Fix by using serde with #[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", deny_unknown_fields)] and return validation errors for unknown variants. Add tests that pass unknown enum and assert 400 with explanation. Also run cargo clippy and add exhaustive matches where possible.

Long: Long-running maintenance: remove all occurrences of feature = "experimental" and tidy up doc comments referencing old endpoints. Also update the changelog and migration notes in docs. Steps:
1) grep for 'experimental' and list files
2) remove cfg attributes and compile
3) run cargo test and fix any resulting compile errors
4) update docs/ to reflect remaining stable endpoints

Provide a small script to automate the grep and run the compile check so future removals are easier. Ensure commit includes changelog entry and updated OpenAPI spec.
Create a Windows MSI installer build step using WiX for our PyQt app and add it to the CI pipeline (artifact signing should be a separate job).
Package the app as a DMG on macOS with a proper .app bundle structure, include a README and license, and ensure icon and background are set.
Add auto-update support (delta updates) using our update server; implement a small updater binary that can atomically replace the app executable on Windows.
Build a portable ZIP release for Linux that doesn't require installation — ensure the bundled SQLite DB is stored under ~/.myapp or XDG_DATA_HOME, not inside the app dir.
Add code signing step (Apple notarization + Developer ID) for macOS releases and document the required certificates in the repo README.
Create a Dockerfile for headless build environment to produce reproducible PyInstaller artifacts for Linux and Windows (using wine for cross-compilation).
Switch the CI packaging from PyInstaller to briefcase (BeeWare) for better macOS native bundle support and test the resulting .app and .msi artifacts.
Update the setup to include an offline installer option that bundles all Python wheels and binary dependencies to support air-gapped deployments.
Ensure the app's SQLite DB schema migrates automatically on first run after an update; add migration scripts and a version check in startup code.
Add a 'portable mode' flag so that when a user places the exe in a folder the app writes config and DB locally (for USB installs) — implement detection in startup.
Fix exporter: On frozen Windows builds, resource files (icons, templates) are missing. Use pkg_resources or sys._MEIPASS to load bundled data at runtime.
Add an installer preflight check that verifies the target machine has the VC++ 2015-2019 runtime; if missing, prompt to install or bundle runtime installer.
Add Linux AppImage packaging and integrate it into the release pipeline. Ensure FUSE dependency is documented and test on Ubuntu 18.04 and 20.04.
Add installer uninstall support that removes created shortcuts, autostart entries, and registered protocol handlers on Windows.
Provide delta update logic server-side: build and store patch files between versions and document API endpoints the updater will call to fetch patches.
Add a CI job that creates deb and rpm packages for Debian/RedHat distributions with correct dependencies and systemd unit files for optional background syncing.
Update the macOS packaging to request hardened runtime entitlements needed for network access and file-system access, and add entitlements plist to repo.
Add a mechanism to rotate log files on install/update and ensure the installer doesn't preserve huge log files (>100MB) when upgrading to new releases.
Add telemetry consent prompt on first-run after installing via MSI/PKG, and persist the user's opt-in choice to a per-user config location.
Add support for auto-elevated updater on Windows (UAC) so that updates that change files in Program Files succeed — implement a separate elevated helper.
Create a signed chocolatey package for Windows to make enterprise deployment easier and add instructions for internal package repository hosting.
Improve our installer to create per-user and per-machine install options and clearly document how to select each via command-line switches for silent install.
Make sure our build produces PDB or dSYM debug symbols for crash reporting and upload them to Sentry in the release pipeline.
Investigate why the frozen app crashes on startup on Linux with ImportError: libGL.so.1 missing. Adjust packaging to bundle libGL or add it as dependency in AppImage.
Add instructions and scripts for enterprise deploy using SCCM/Intune, including silent install args, detection method, and uninstall string.
When building with PyInstaller, the multiprocessing module fails with 'RuntimeError: Sentry SDK reimported'. Reproduce happens only in frozen build — investigate and fix.
Add a CLI flag --no-updates for admins to deploy a locked version and prevent auto-updater from running after install; persist to config with clear precedence rules.
Document deployment prerequisites for each platform in DEPLOYMENT.md: required runtime versions, certificate setup, updater endpoints, and firewall rules.
Add a release pipeline step that verifies GUI loads in xvfb for Linux headless builds and runs a smoke test that opens main window and exits cleanly.
Add a simple REST health-check endpoint to the local embedded HTTP API (used by the tray/updater) so the external update service can verify running versions.
Short: Add Windows start menu shortcut creation to installer.
Short: Include license.txt in the root of packaged .app and installers.
Short: Add CI job to upload artifacts to GitHub Releases automatically.
Short: Ensure the app uses the system proxy settings when checking for updates.
Short: Add a hash verification step on update downloads to prevent corrupted installs.
Short: Create a 'silent install' command-line option for MSI that accepts install dir and user scope.
Short: Add crashpad/Breakpad integration so we can collect native crash dumps from frozen builds.
Short: Ensure app's embedded Python is isolated; do not inherit system site-packages in frozen builds.
Short: Include a README.txt in Windows installers with quick start and support contact.

Medium: When we roll out v3.2.0, users report the app failing to start on macOS Catalina with a Gatekeeper block. We need to add a notarization step and update installer docs. Also include troubleshooting steps for users to bypass Gatekeeper (spctl command) and add CI job to notarize and staple the ticket.

Medium: Our CI pipeline currently builds a single artifact per OS. Add matrix jobs to build for multiple Python versions (3.9, 3.10, 3.11) and produce named artifacts (myapp-3.9-win64.exe, etc.). Ensure packaging script picks correct interpreter for extension modules.

Medium: The updater service is returning 500 for some requests intermittently. Provide a retry/backoff in the client with exponential backoff and a max retry count. Log failures to a local update.log and provide a way to manually trigger update check from settings.

Medium: On Linux installs via .deb, our app installs under /opt/myapp but we forgot to include a systemd user service for background sync on per-user installs. Add a systemd unit template and postinst script that registers the user service when --enable-autostart is set.

Medium: After bundling with PyInstaller, some optional C extensions (cryptography) fail to import. We should explicitly include the wheels or dynamic libs in the spec file and test importing cryptography in the frozen exe. Also document how to rebuild c-ext dependencies in CI.

Medium: Add verification of downloaded signatures when auto-updating: downloads should be accompanied by detached GPG signatures that the updater validates using an embedded public key. Document key rotation policy for deployment.

Medium: Installer is not creating a desktop shortcut for users on Linux (Gnome). Update the .desktop file installation and use xdg-desktop-menu to register the shortcut, ensuring correct Exec path from installation directory.

Medium: We need to support proxy authentication for the updater on corporate networks. Add reading of system proxy settings and allow overriding via config file (proxy host, username, password — store encrypted).

Medium: When packaging the app, the bundled SQLite extension (FTS5) is missing on certain Linux distros causing DB errors. Add a runtime check to verify SQLite features and fallback to pure-Python search or fail gracefully with clear message.
Medium: Add a signed update manifest endpoint with changelogs; updater should only accept manifests signed by our release key. Add unit tests that validate the signature verification code path.

Medium: Add a Windows installer option to register custom URI scheme (myapp://) and set up protocol handler to launch the app and pass URL to a command-line handler. Ensure proper registry keys and uninstall cleanup.

Long: We're getting intermittent crash reports from macOS users after upgrading to a notarized build. Crash log extract:

Process:               MyApp [1234]
Path:                  /Applications/MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp
Identifier:            com.example.myapp
Version:               3.4.1 (3410)
Code Type:             X86-64 (Native)
Parent Process:        ??? [1]

Crashed Thread:        0 Dispatch queue: com.apple.main-thread
Exception Type:        EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Codes:       KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000010

Thread 0 Crashed:: Dispatch queue: com.apple.main-thread
0   _objc_msgSend_ptrs + 16
1   QtCore                 0x000000010a7c1234 QMetaObject::activate(QObject*, int, int, void**) + 276
2   QtWidgets              0x000000010bb0abcd QWidget::closeEvent(QCloseEvent*) + 88
3   MyApp                  0x000000010c0b1a3f main + 1023

This mainly affects users who upgraded from a non-notarized build. Repro steps: install older non-notarized 3.3.x, then update to 3.4.x via auto-update on Big Sur. Possible cause: mismatched Qt plugin or signed bundle missing plugin signatures. Please add detailed debug logs around plugin loads and ensure we notarize the entire .app with all nested frameworks and plugins, and include a script to check codesign -vvv on bundle.

Long: After packaging with PyInstaller, some users on Windows get this traceback when launching the app:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "site-packages\PyQt5\Qt\bin\pythonqt.dll", line 0, in <module>
  File "main.py", line 12, in <module>
    from gui.main_window import MainWindow
  File "gui\main_window.py", line 8, in <module>
    from resources import icons
  File "resources\icons.py", line 3, in <module>
    ICON_PATH = Path(sys._MEIPASS) / 'icons'  # fails when not frozen
AttributeError: module 'sys' has no attribute '_MEIPASS'

Reproduction: freeze with PyInstaller on Python 3.9. Possible fix: guard resource loading with getattr(sys, '_MEIPASS', None) and fallback to importlib.resources for non-frozen dev runs. Update spec to include icons folder as datas. Add code example:

import sys
from pathlib import Path

def get_resource_path(relative):
    base = getattr(sys, '_MEIPASS', Path(__file__).parent)
    return Path(base) / relative

Also add CI tests that run the frozen exe on a Windows runner and import gui.main_window to ensure resources load.

Long: We're seeing failing updates with a TLS handshake error on Windows clients behind a corporate proxy. Error log from updater:

2025-10-12 09:14:03,412 - updater - ERROR - Failed to check for updates
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='updates.example.com', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /manifest.json (Caused by SSLError(SSLEOFError(8, 'EOF occurred in violation of protocol (_ssl.c:1131)')))

Repro: In corp network, set system proxy and try manual update. The requests library in our embedded Python doesn't pick up Windows system certificate store, causing validation failures. Proposed fixes: configure requests to use certifi bundle shipped with app, and add logic to load CA certs from OS cert store on Windows (using certifi-win32 or certifi where needed). Also add a proxy auth prompt and allow specifying proxy exceptions. Example change:

import requests
import certifi

session = requests.Session()
session.verify = certifi.where()
# optionally load additional CA file from registry path if present

Add tests using mitmproxy in CI to simulate TLS interception and ensure behavior is as expected.

Long: After latest update, the app can't open the bundled encrypted settings file. Stack trace from startup:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/startup.py", line 32, in <module>
    settings = Settings.load()
  File "app/settings.py", line 210, in load
    data = decrypt_file(settings_path, key)
  File "app/crypto.py", line 45, in decrypt_file
    cipher = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_GCM, nonce=nonce)
ValueError: Incorrect IV length (it must be 16 bytes long)

This only happens on frozen builds (PyInstaller) on Windows. Dev builds (python main.py) work fine. Hypothesis: during packaging we truncated the binary settings blob or changed padding. Steps to reproduce: 1) Package app with PyInstaller spec including --onefile, 2) run app, 3) try to import existing user profile from %APPDATA%\MyApp\settings.bin. Suggestion: stop using --onefile for now (split on-disk resources) or ensure we preserve binary mode when bundling. Also add unit tests for encryption/decryption round trip using the exact packaging runtime (use pytest + tox to run tests with tox target that simulates frozen runtime).

Long: Windows launchers fail for some users with error dialog 'The application was unable to start correctly (0xc000007b)'. Event Viewer shows:

Faulting application name: MyApp.exe, version: 3.5.0.0, time stamp: 0x5f8c1234
Faulting module name: KERNELBASE.dll, version: 10.0.19041.867, time stamp: 0x5076f45d
Exception code: 0xc000007b

This usually indicates mixing 32-bit and 64-bit DLLs. Build matrix: Python 3.10 x64, PyInstaller hooks bundle several binary wheels (libEGL, libGLES, Qt5Core.dll). Some of our dependencies (a custom native DLL) were built for x86. Request: audit all bundled DLLs in the dist folder, ensure they match target arch, and add CI verification script that checks PE headers for machine type. Example script snippet to check PE architecture:

import pefile
for path in dist_dir.rglob('*.dll'):
    pe = pefile.PE(str(path))
    print(path, hex(pe.FILE_HEADER.Machine))

Add remediation: rebuild native extension for x64 and update packaging pipeline.

Long: The auto-update process seems to leave app in inconsistent state when an update fails midway. Reproduction steps and logs:

1. App downloads patch file update-3.6.patch (50MB)
2. Verifies SHA256 OK
3. Launches updater.exe to apply patch and exits main app
4. updater during apply fails with disk IO error (No space left)
5. updater crashes, leaving partial files under C:\Program Files\MyApp\_tmp
6. Next launch, app reports 'binary corrupted' and refuses to start

We need an atomic update strategy: apply update into temporary dir, validate everything, then move new files over old ones using an atomic rename where possible, and implement rollback on failure. Also implement disk space calculation before download, and show user-friendly message if insufficient. Example pseudo-code for update apply:

# download -> tmp_dir
# verify hash/signature
# extract to tmp_dir/extracted
# run quick smoke tests (import critical modules)
# if OK: move current_dir -> backup_dir; move tmp_dir/extracted -> current_dir
# on move error: restore from backup_dir
# finally remove backup_dir

Also update installer to keep previous version for one update to support rollback and add unit/integration tests simulating IO errors during move to ensure rollback succeeds.

Long: On startup, the app tries to create the database in app bundle path which fails on macOS when installed in /Applications (read-only). Error trace:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/__main__.py", line 14, in <module>
    db = Database.connect(DB_PATH)
  File "app/db.py", line 55, in connect
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file

We need to change default DB location to a writeable per-user path (~/Library/Application Support/MyApp/db.sqlite3 on macOS, %APPDATA% on Windows, XDG_DATA_HOME on Linux). Migration steps: on first run after update, copy existing DB from bundle or system location to user data dir and update config path. Also change installer to not pre-create DB in app bundle. Provide code snippet for path resolution:

from pathlib import Path
import appdirs

data_dir = Path(appdirs.user_data_dir('MyApp', 'ExampleCorp'))
data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
db_path = data_dir / 'db.sqlite3'

Add migration unit tests and update release notes about data migration.

Long: We're packaging the app for Linux using Snap and some users report it can't access local files outside home directory with PermissionDenied errors. Example error in logs:

PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/mnt/data/project'

Snap's confinement blocks access. Options: 1) declare plugs and request classic confinement, 2) use interfaces like personal-files and removable-media in snapcraft.yaml, or 3) document limitations and provide flatpak or deb alternative. Proposed fix: add necessary plugs (home, removable-media) and educate users on connecting interfaces (snap connect). Also review code that uses absolute paths and prefer asking user via file picker (which Snap allows through portals). Include snapcraft.yaml snippet and testing steps on Ubuntu Core and desktop Ubuntu.

Long: On Windows, the installer fails when MSI property INSTALLDIR contains non-ASCII characters (e.g., user's name with accents). MSI log shows:

MSI (s) (E8:48) [10:33:05:123]: Product: MyApp -- Error 1327.The drive:\path\to\folder is invalid

Investigation: our setup uses char encoding assumptions and the bundled installer exe doesn't handle Unicode paths when creating shortcuts or writing registry keys. Request: ensure WiX project uses Unicode and that all paths are wrapped properly, test on systems with non-ASCII user folders, and update installer to store per-user config under %LOCALAPPDATA% instead of path containing the Installer's path. Also add automated tests on GitHub Actions runner with locale set to es_ES or ru_RU to catch regressions.

Long: The app's tray updater fails to start on login when installed per-user. Debug logs from Windows event viewer:

Application: MyApp.Tray.exe
Framework Version: v4.0.30319
Description: The process was terminated due to an unhandled exception.
Exception Info: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the registry key 'HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' is denied.

We've been creating a registry Run key during installer run as admin, which fails for per-user installs. Fix: during per-user install, write the run key to HKCU instead of HKLM; for machine installs use HKLM. Additionally, offer an in-app toggle for autostart that writes to correct scope and handles errors gracefully. Provide PowerShell snippet to add/remove run key and update installer to call those scripts depending on install scope.

Long: After deployment we keep getting user reports that app can't find SSL cert bundle for requests and fails with certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate. Example exception:

requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1123)

This occurs on macOS and Windows when users run system Python builds; in our frozen distribution the bundled certifi cert bundle path isn't resolved. Fix: vendor certifi and set requests' session.verify to certifi.where() on startup. For macOS/Windows, provide fallback to load macOS keychain certs or to allow admin to install root CA. Add code example:

import requests
import certifi

session = requests.Session()
session.verify = certifi.where()

Also add a diagnostic in the app 'Check network' that displays the cert bundle path and sample TLS handshake result (CN, issuer) to assist support.

Long: The signed Mac installer fails notarization because the nested frameworks inside the .app are unsigned. Notarization log excerpt:

ERROR: ios notarization failed
Error Messages:
- The binary at "MyApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/QtCore.framework/Versions/5/QtCore" is not signed.

Fix: ensure codesign signs all nested frameworks and helper executables before stapling. Add a sign_and_notarize.sh script that recursively signs frameworks and helpers and verifies with codesign --verify --deep --strict before submitting to altool. Add build CI step that runs codesign verification and halts if verification fails. Provide sample script pattern:

codesign --force --timestamp --options runtime --entitlements entitlements.plist -s 'Developer ID Application: Example' "$FRAMEWORK"
codesign --verify --deep --strict "$APP_BUNDLE"

Document certificate installation on CI runner and gate the step behind secrets.

Long: Packaging for Alpine Linux fails due to musl vs glibc mismatch when we include prebuilt wheels that link to glibc. Error from ldd shows missing GLIBC_2.28 symbols and app crashes on import of extension module. Example error:

ImportError: /usr/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pylibfoo.so: undefined symbol: GLIBC_2.28

We need to produce distro-appropriate builds: either build manylinux wheels for Linux glibc or use a static linking strategy for extensions. For Alpine, consider building inside a musl-based builder or switch to a tar.gz distribution that uses system Python and lists package dependencies. Add CI job that runs test run on Alpine Docker and ensures extension modules import cleanly. Document supported distros in deployment docs and provide fallback instructions for admins to install glibc compatibility layer if needed.

Long: During packaging, the app's embedded HTTP API port (53000) conflicts with other services in some customers' environments and updater fails to start. Currently we hardcode the port in code:

DEFAULT_PORT = 53000
server.bind(('127.0.0.1', DEFAULT_PORT))

Request: make port configurable via environment variable MYAPP_PORT and add logic to try next available ports if configured port is occupied, with exponential backoff retries. Also expose the chosen port via the tray icon and update the installer to allow setting a fixed port for locked-down environments. Provide code example:

import socket

def acquire_port(preferred=None):
    for p in ([preferred] + list(range(53000, 53010))):
        if p is None: continue
        with socket.socket() as s:
            try:
                s.bind(('127.0.0.1', p))
                return p
            except OSError:
                continue
    raise RuntimeError('No free ports')

Add tests simulating port collisions.

Long: The updater downloads and extracts zip updates but on macOS the extracted .app loses executable permissions leading to 'operation not permitted' on launch. Extraction log:

Unzipping update-3.7.zip to /tmp/update_extracted
Setting permissions on MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp -> failed: [Errno 13] Permission denied

We should preserve chmods in zip or better use tar.gz for macOS to preserve executable bits. When using zip, after extraction ensure we set executable permission bits for binaries using os.chmod. Also ensure the updater runs chown/chmod as appropriate if it runs under a different user. Provide code snippet:

import stat
for path in Path(extracted).rglob('Contents/MacOS/*'):
    mode = path.stat().st_mode
    path.chmod(mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH)

Add CI test that unpacks on macOS runner and verifies main binary is executable.

Long: Users report that when the app is distributed via an enterprise .msi with the per-machine option, the embedded HTTP API binds only to 127.0.0.1 and remote management tools can't reach it. We currently do:

HOST = '127.0.0.1'
server.bind((HOST, port))

For enterprise deployments we should allow binding to 0.0.0.0 via an installer flag, but warn about security implications and restrict remote access to localhost unless explicitly enabled with TLS and auth. Add installer UI and silent install flag /BINDHOST=0.0.0.0, implement token-based auth if bind != 127.0.0.1, and update docs. Provide an example config and recommended firewall rules. Also add a CI integration test that starts server bound to 0.0.0.0 and verifies remote connection using curl with the token header.

Long: Some users on Windows see AV/Defender quarantine the installer executable claiming 'Potentially Unwanted Application'. This blocks automated deployment. We should reduce false positives by minimizing bundled installers, ensuring proper code signing, and submitting false positive reports to major AV vendors. Also implement an enterprise distribution channel (signed MSI via SCCM) and include a notary hash in release notes so admins can verify before deploying. Add guidance in DEPLOYMENT.md for IT admins on whitelisting hashes and certificates and add a preflight script to compute and display sha256sum of artifacts.
Add support for configurable log rotation by size and age to the file logger (currently only time-based rotation exists).
Expose a hook interface so external systems can receive structured log entries for correlation IDs.
Make the default logger non-global; provide a NewLogger(ctx, cfg) constructor to avoid package-level state.
Add support for JSON-encoded logs with optional pretty-print flag for local development.
Add a Prometheus collector that exports counts of log levels (debug/info/warn/error) per service.
Enable lazy evaluation of expensive log fields (like fmt.Sprintf) via a FieldFunc type.
Provide a way to inject request-scoped context values (trace_id, user_id) into every log entry automatically.
Add a small middleware for HTTP servers that adds an incremental request counter metric and latency histogram.
Support output to multiple writers (stdout + file + remote) with independent formatters and levels.
Add a CheckExists method to the config loader that validates all logging sinks are reachable at startup.
Normalize timestamp formatting to RFC3339Nano and make it configurable per-sink.
Fix a race when swapping logger configuration at runtime; calls to Logger.With() panic intermittently.
Add a test helper that asserts a log message with specific fields was emitted during unit tests.
Provide a way to drop PII fields from logs based on a redaction list at the logger level.
Allow toggling stacktrace capture per log level; stack traces are expensive at info level by default.
Add native support for OpenTelemetry traces injection into logs (trace_id, span_id) when context contains traces.
Support sampling of logs by key (e.g., sample 1% of debug logs per trace_id) to reduce volume.
Document and export the internal severity constants so they can be used by downstream packages.
Add a zapcore.Core adapter so the library can be used as a sink for zap easily.
Add backpressure handling for the async log buffer; when disk/remote sinks are slow, provide a drop strategy.
Improve README with a getting-started example showing how to integrate with Gin and net/http.
Rename package logger to slog for clarity and avoid clashes with other common logger packages.
Provide an io.Writer adapter that converts stdlib log.Logger output into structured events for this library.
Make the library's errors implement Unwrap so callers can check underlying errors using errors.Is/As.
Add a CLI tool to tail logs from a local file sink with filtering by level and field matchers.
Expose metrics for dropped logs and queue length when using the async writer.
Add tests covering concurrency for WithField on the global logger to verify no data races.
Add ability to set a maximum size for in-memory log buffer per goroutine to avoid OOMs under high load.
Integrate with systemd journald socket when running on Linux to write native journal entries.
Make the logger's JSON encoder escape HTML by default for browser-consumable logs, configurable via option.
Short: Add a builder for Field objects to reduce boilerplate.
