Request: allow passing plain mappings or dataclasses by detecting dataclasses.is_dataclass(obj) and using dataclasses.asdict(obj), and support pydantic.BaseModel via .dict(). Add unit tests and update docs to show interoperability examples.
Add automatic header injection for traceparent W3C header and expose an option to disable it per-client. Provide integration test verifying header propagation through internal service calls.
Replace unsafe gets() usage in the UI input dialog with fgets() and proper buffer size checks.
Harden IPC channel between main process and plugin subprocess: add message length checks and reject malformed headers.
Validate and sanitize file paths passed to the exporter to prevent directory traversal when saving user-selected files.
Require privilege separation for the updater: run update download in unprivileged process and verify signatures before replacing binaries.
Add CSRF-like token for internal HTTP-based settings UI to prevent local web UI request forgery.
Avoid storing plaintext API keys in preferences file; encrypt with OS keyring or use DPAPI/KWallet where available.
Replace sprintf() calls in the networking module with snprintf() and check return values to prevent buffer overflows.
Audit use of system() and popen(); migrate shell calls to execv() family or platform APIs that avoid shell interpretation.
Add strict certificate pinning for the app's remote config fetch to prevent MITM tampering of configuration.
Limit maximum uploaded attachment size in the chat widget and validate Content-Type and magic bytes before processing.
Add sandboxing for plugin DLL loading on Windows by checking signatures and using a restricted token before LoadLibrary.
Fix race condition in session cache flushing: use mutex around cache writes to disk to avoid corrupted session files.
Add timeout and retry policy for network requests to config server; include exponential backoff and jitter.
Replace custom crypto with well-known libs (OpenSSL/Botan) and ensure we use authenticated encryption (AES-GCM) for stored blobs.
Strip leading/trailing whitespace and normalize Unicode in filenames before saving to disk to avoid confusing path comparisons.
Ensure the preferences export feature redacts sensitive fields (passwords, tokens) before writing to the clipboard or file.
Add input validation on plugin API: require explicit version and capability negotiation to prevent ABI confusion from third-party modules.
Eliminate double-free in image decoder by checking reference counts before freeing in the cleanup path.
Move debug logging that prints access tokens behind a flag and never log them at INFO level in production builds.
Use secure RNG (getrandom()/CryptGenRandom) for session ID generation instead of rand() seeded with time().
Fix unchecked return values in file read code; handle partial reads and EOF gracefully in the settings loader (fread/ferror checks).
Restrict D-Bus interface exposure: only expose required methods and validate callers via credentials when possible.
On Windows, enable DEP/NX and ASLR build flags for release binaries and document the build script changes for CI.
Harden plugin handshake: implement HMAC of handshake payload using shared secret negotiated at install time.
Detect and reject symlink-based attacks when saving project files: ensure realpath(parent) matches expected directories.
Add user confirmation and permission prompt before allowing external applications to open app deep links.
Sanitize format strings passed to the logging wrapper to prevent format string exploits from untrusted input.
Prevent integer overflow when calculating allocation size for image buffers: check dimensions before malloc.
Add a safe fallback for missing certificate chain when contacting update server: fail closed and show UI error.
Ensure config files created by the app are created with 600 permissions on POSIX and restrict ACLs on Windows.

Medium: The CLI integration allows passing a file path that eventually reaches execv for an external tool. We should validate the file path is within the project directory and ensure no shell expansion or environment variable injection happens. Consider canonicalizing with realpath() and refusing paths that escape sandbox roots.

Medium: Our settings import feature currently trusts JSON fields blindly. Attackers could embed long strings to cause mem allocations or unexpected values. Add size limits, validate types, and reject unknown top-level keys. Also add unit tests that feed malformed JSON to the parser and assert safe failures.

Medium: The image rendering pipeline uses libpng and doesn't check return codes on png_read_update_info. We observed corrupted PNGs leading to crashes. Add error checks, validate chunk lengths, and catch libpng errors with setjmp/longjmp handling appropriate for desktop GUI thread models.

Medium: On Linux the app creates a local HTTP endpoint for OAuth redirect. If an attacker can bind to that port first, they can intercept tokens. Change to use ephemeral loopback-only sockets and verify the received state parameter matches the nonce generated by the app. Consider binding to 127.0.0.1 only and random high ports.

Medium: The update downloader accepts redirect responses without validating Location header. This allowed redirection to internal network addresses in tests. Add host whitelisting and validate that redirects stay on allowed hostnames or use the original host to refuse cross-host redirects.

Medium: Crash on malformed .ini files during parsing causes a buffer overflow. Rework parser to use strnlen checks, limit section/key lengths to 256 bytes, and handle non-ASCII characters safely. Add fuzzing inputs in CI to catch regressions.

Medium: When we deserialize saved window layouts, we call malloc with user-provided width*height which overflowed on large values. Add checks to ensure width and height are within sane ranges before computing size and handle allocation failures gracefully.

Medium: The plugin loader enumerates plugin directories and loads any .so/.dll present. Add signature verification and a plugin manifest with author & version metadata; refuse unsigned plugins in release mode. Also sandbox plugin process and restrict environment variables passed in.

Medium: The app uses HTTP Basic Auth to talk to the sync server over plain HTTP in a corporate network. Upgrade client to always use HTTPS and reject insecure endpoints unless explicitly allowed with a user-visible warning and admin override.

Medium: We log the full stack trace to the user.log on crashes, which includes file paths and environment variables. Limit logged information in release builds and mask secrets (API keys, tokens) before writing crash dumps. Provide a secure upload workflow for diagnostics with explicit consent.

Medium: On Windows, stored credentials are saved in an unprotected file under %APPDATA%. Use CryptProtectData (DPAPI) for encrypting per-user secrets and provide a migration path for existing files. Document fallback if DPAPI is unavailable.
Medium: During authentication, we compare HMACs using memcmp which is timing-vulnerable. Replace with constant-time comparison function for all MAC and password checks to avoid timing leak attacks.

Medium: The app supports remote control via a TCP socket bound to 0.0.0.0 by default on older installs. Change default to 127.0.0.1 and require explicit opt-in for remote bindings. Add authentication on the control socket and rate limits.
Medium: The
Fix event emitter leak: subscribers to 'data' are not removed on dispose(), causing memory growth during long-lived connections.
Correct type exports in index.js to preserve default export for CommonJS consumers (currently breaks require('lib').default).
Fix race condition in debounce implementation where flush() can call the handler twice under heavy concurrency.
Update cookie-setting helper to include SameSite=None and secure when running on HTTPS, otherwise Safari 13 blocks login.
Ensure module uses strict equality (===) in diff algorithm to avoid false positives when comparing 0 and '0'.
Handle null response in parseJSON helper — JSON.parse throws when response body is empty; should return null instead.
Fix SSR hydration mismatch: library renders inconsistent class order between server and client, causing React to warn on hydration.
Prevent double-await bug in async map: when mapper returns a Promise that resolves synchronously, we sometimes await twice and lose stack traces.
Make internal cache TTL configurable — currently items expire instantly due to negative default TTL.
Fix broken source maps in production build so stack traces map to original files (sourcemap path generation incorrect).
The router's push() silently swallows navigation errors when History.pushState fails (QuotaExceededError on Safari). Propagate the error to caller.
Buffer overflow in binary serializer when serializing large ArrayBuffers — adjust chunking logic to stream rather than allocate whole buffer.
Fix fallback for missing Intl.RelativeTimeFormat to include a polyfill check so older browsers don't crash.
Correctly escape user input in template rendering to prevent XSS when using backticks in content.
Fix file upload progress emitter: bytesTotal is undefined on multipart/form-data requests, causing NaN percent calculations.
Resolve regression where asyncIterator is not marked Symbol.asyncIterator — breaks for-await-of loops.
The retry middleware uses setTimeout with stringified delay, causing delays to default to 0. Convert to Number.
Prevent infinite loop in binary search when low and high indices are floating — ensure integer floor/ceil rounding.
Fix network error categorization: 502 and 503 should be retried by default but are classified as fatal.
Ensure deep clone preserves Dates and RegExps instead of converting them to plain objects.
Fix memory leak where DOM nodes appended via patch() retain references in vnode caches after removal.
The default logger swallows Errors with no message; change to log stack if available so debugging has context.
Add guard in setState to batch updates properly when setState called during render; currently throws 'setState during render' in React concurrent mode.
Fix pagination cursor encoding in REST client: base64 padding stripped causing 400s on decode in backend.
Ensure CSS-in-JS injects critical styles before head end to avoid FOUC on slow networks.
Fix optional chaining fallback implementation so that it doesn't silently swallow undefined accessors that should throw in strict mode.
Restore promise cancellation token behavior previously removed — callers rely on cancel() to stop background tasks.
Improve error message when plugin registration fails: include plugin id and current plugin map state for debugging.
Fix capitalization bug in locales lookup: 'en-us' and 'en-US' should map to the same locale data file.
Fix token refresh race: multiple concurrent requests trigger parallel refresh attempts. Introduce single-flight refresh lock.
Fix malformed Content-Type for JSON responses in server-side rendering helper; currently appends charset twice.
Fix incorrect iteration order for Map-like structures in serialize() — iteration currently uses object keys and loses insertion order.
Prevent unhandled promise rejection when websocket.onmessage handler throws — wrap callbacks and reject gracefully with context.
Fix isomorphic fetch wrapper to use globalThis.fetch when available; current check breaks in new workers where window is undefined.
Fix AES encryption helper to properly handle non-utf8 passphrases (use TextEncoder) — encrypted payloads were corrupted across platforms.
Fix cursor leak in database adapter: db.query opens client but never releases it in certain error paths.
Fix CSS class deduplication so scoped classes don't collide across different components during hot-reload.
Correct date formatting in localization utility to respect locale-specific week start (Sunday vs Monday).
Fix slow initial render by deferring expensive layout calculations to requestIdleCallback on supported browsers.
Fix missing Content-Length header in file downloads served through the library's static handler, causing some browsers to hang.
Address tree-shaking regression: library side-effect flag in package.json is incorrectly set, bundlers include unused code.
Fix debounce immediate flag behavior: immediate=true should call on leading edge but currently calls on both leading and trailing edges.
Fix null propagation in query builder: .where('x', null) should generate IS NULL, not = 'null'.
Fix inconsistent behavior for toString override in vdom nodes that caused concatenation with numbers to produce 'object Object'.
Fix Promise.allSettled polyfill to match spec: each result object should have status: 'fulfilled' || 'rejected' and value/reason keys.
Fix caching header generation to include Vary: Accept-Language when responses differ by locale.
Fix circular dependency crash in module loader — detect cycles and return a partial module object per CommonJS spec.
Fix event delegation when root element is removed during event handling; ensure listeners don't access detached elements.
Fix CLI build command to respect NODE_ENV=production for minifier config — currently uses development mode.
Fix TypeScript declaration for middleware composition: next parameter should be typed as () => Promise<void> not any to improve dev DX.

Long: Intermittent 'Cannot read property 'children' of undefined' in virtual DOM diffing on route change

We get this stack trace occasionally when navigating quickly between routes in the demo app:

TypeError: Cannot read property 'children' of undefined
    at diffChildren (lib/vdom/diff.js:128:22)
    at diffNode (lib/vdom/diff.js:84:18)
    at applyPatch (lib/vdom/patch.js:45:12)
    at update (lib/app/update.js:62:10)

Reproduction steps:
1. Open demo and navigate to /infinite-list
2. Scroll quickly to load more items (infinite loader triggers)
3. Click a different route before the asynchronous load resolves

Hypothesis: when the async loaded data resolves, the reconciler is still diffing the old tree and expects node.children to exist. We should guard diffChildren against undefined nodes and check that node.type matches before accessing children. Possible fix: add a null check at the start of diffChildren and bail out if nodes differ by identity/type.

Relevant code snippet:

function diffChildren(oldNode, newNode) {
  const oldChildren = oldNode.children; // <-- error occurs here when oldNode undefined
  // ...
}

Please add a guard and unit test that reproduces the fast-route-change scenario using fake timers.

Long: Localization datetime formatting off by one hour in certain timezones

Description:
When formatting dates with our library's wrapper around Intl.DateTimeFormat, events scheduled during DST transitions are off by one hour for users in Europe/Berlin and America/Sao_Paulo. The underlying code constructs dates from parts incorrectly and uses Date.UTC without considering local offset properly.

Failing code:

function formatLocal(dateString, locale) {
  const d = new Date(dateString); // input like '2023-03-26T01:30:00'
  const parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { hour: 'numeric', minute: 'numeric', timeZoneName: 'short' }).formatToParts(d);
  return parts.map(p => p.value).join('');
}

Cases:
- DST start in Europe/Berlin: 2023-03-26 02:00 does not exist; creating new Date('2023-03-26T02:30:00') rolls into next valid time causing shift

Proposed changes:
- Use Temporal API polyfill if available for wall-clock arithmetic, or use date-fns-tz to parse in given timezone explicitly.
- Add tests for DST boundary times and ensure displayed time matches calendar selection.

Please add timezone-aware parsing and fallback to current implementation if polyfills are not loaded, but emit a warning when formatting DST-edge times without timezone awareness.

Long: Mobile Safari throws QUOTA_EXCEEDED_ERR when writing to localStorage on private mode

Issue:
Some users report errors when the library tries to cache metadata to localStorage during initialization on iOS Safari Private Browsing. The operation throws QuotaExceededError and crashes initialization.

Error example:

DOMException: The operation is insecure.
    at Object.setItem (native)
    at Cache.set (lib/cache/local.js:23:12)

Current code:

class LocalCache {
  set(key, val) { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(val)); }
  get(key) { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key)); }
}

Fix:
- Wrap localStorage operations in try/catch and fall back to in-memory Map when storage unavailable.
- Add feature-detect function isLocalStorageAvailable() that tries to set and remove a test key.

Also ensure initialization continues gracefully if cache fails, and emit a warning. Add tests simulating DOMException when setItem is called.

Long: Sorting comparator in table component treats numeric strings incorrectly

Problem:
The table's client-side sort comparator compares values via localeCompare which treats numbers as strings causing '10' to come before '2'. This breaks numeric columns where values can be numeric strings (from CSV import).

Current comparator:

function compare(a, b) {
  return String(a).localeCompare(String(b));
}

Desired behavior:
- Detect numbers (parseFloat and isFinite) and sort numerically
- Fallback to localeCompare for non-numeric

Edge cases:
- Mixed numeric and non-numeric values in same column (e.g., 'N/A') -> non-numeric should sort after numbers when ascending
- Negative numbers and decimals

Please update comparator to coerce numeric strings to numbers when both values are numeric, otherwise use localeCompare. Add unit tests for cases: ['2','10'], ['10','2','N/A'], ['-1','0','1.5'] and ensure sort stability.

Long: Custom serializer for DateRange loses timezone information

Context:
Library serializes DateRange objects for storage and transport with format { start: Date, end: Date }. The serializer converts Dates to ISO strings via date.toISOString() which normalizes to UTC. Consumers expect to preserve original timezone offset for display. This causes UX bugs when the client local timezone differs from server timezone.

Example:
const range = { start: new Date('2023-11-01T09:00:00-05:00'), end: new Date('2023-11-01T17:00:00-05:00') };
serialize(range) -> { start: '2023-11-01T14:00:00.000Z', end: '2023-11-01T22:00:00.000Z' }

When deserialized in timezone -05:00, UI shows 09:00 correctly but library's date-creation logic uses Date constructor which may lose original textual timezone string.

Proposed approach:
- Preserve original timezone offset by serializing to { iso: d.toISOString(), tzOffset: d.getTimezoneOffset() } or store RFC3339 with offset using date.toString() or a dedicated format like 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZZ'.
- When deserializing, reconstruct using a timezone-aware parser (date-fns-tz parseISO with timezone offset) or store both iso and original string.

Add tests ensuring original timezone offset survives round-trip and UI display matches original local time.

Long: SVG icon loader strips viewBox attribute leading to scaling issues

We inline SVGs to allow CSS fill overrides. After recent change, our SVG loader strips attributes considered unsafe; it removes viewBox from some SVGs causing icons to stretch when width/height are set.

Example broken SVG snippet:
<svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24">...</svg>

After loader sanitization it becomes:
<svg width="24" height="24">...</svg>

Impact:
- Icons no longer scale correctly on high-DPI display
- Accessibility tests fail because viewBox required for proper semantics

Loader code does attribute filtering like:
const allowed = ['width', 'height', 'focusable'];

Proposed fix:
- Add 'viewBox' to allowed attributes list
- Ensure case-insensitive matching and preserve original attribute order where possible
- Add a regression test using a fixture SVG with viewBox and assert output contains viewBox

Also ensure sanitization still removes <script> tags and on* attributes to prevent XSS.

Long: Plugin API callback not awaited causing unpredictable teardown order

Issue:
Plugins can implement async init() and teardown() functions. During app shutdown we call plugin.teardown() but do not await returned Promise. This causes subsequent cleanup code to run before plugins finish, leading to race conditions (e.g., closing DB while plugin still using it).

Current shutdown code:

for (const plugin of plugins) {
  if (plugin.teardown) plugin.teardown(); // not awaited
}
cleanupCore();

Observed logs:
Warning: plugin A tried to access DB after it was closed

Proposed fix:
- Treat teardown/init as potentially async and await each (or run Promise.all to parallelize but still await completion)
- Add timeout to prevent forever-hanging teardowns and log plugin id on timeout

Please update shutdown flow to await plugin.teardown() with a configurable per-plugin timeout and add tests for async teardown and timeout handling.

Long: Build output contains duplicate CSS rules after tree-shaking due to side-effectful imports

Problem:
After upgrading to Rollup 3, the final CSS bundle contains duplicated rules from components because CSS modules imported from .js files are treated as side-effectful despite being pure. This duplicates rules when components are tree-shaken and reimported with different import aliases.

Symptoms:
- Production CSS file size doubled
- Visual regressions in specificity

Investigation:
- package.json currently lacks 'sideEffects' field, bundler conservatively includes CSS modules multiple times
- CSS-in-JS extractor assumes each import yields a unique id but duplicates when same file imported via different relative paths

Fixes:
- Add 'sideEffects': false to package.json for JS files and mark CSS files as side-effectful using an allowlist: ["**/*.css"]
- Normalize import path resolution in CSS extractor to use realpath or resolved id
- Deduplicate CSS rules by tracking seen rule hashes during extract

Please implement path normalization and dedupe, update packaging metadata, and verify bundle sizes are reduced with tests simulating duplicate imports.

Long: Error: 'Buffer is not defined' in browser bundle when using Node-only dependency indirectly

Description:
A transitive dependency expects Node Buffer global; our bundler provides a small shim for Buffer only to modules directly imported by the library. However code executed in the browser (worker context) still attempts to access Buffer via globalThis.Buffer and fails with ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined.

Error trace from browser console:
ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined
    at decodeToken (node_modules/jwt-decode/index.js:10:15)
    at eval (src/auth/token.js:22:20)

Root cause:
- Our bundler config marks 'buffer' as external for browser target in certain cases
- We didn't include fallback polyfill or ensure Buffer is injected into global scope

Fix options:
- Add a lightweight Buffer polyfill (buffer from npm) to browser bundle and set globalThis.Buffer = require('buffer').Buffer
- Or refactor code to avoid Node Buffer usage; use atob/Uint8Array for base64 decoding on browser

Please choose the more sustainable approach (avoid shimming Node globals when a web API exists). Replace Buffer usage in token decoding with atob and TextDecoder. Add tests in browser-like environment.

Long: CSS variable fallback not applied due to missing computedStyle retrieval on detached nodes

Issue:
The theming helper resolves CSS custom properties via getComputedStyle(targetElement).getPropertyValue('--color-primary'). When called early for elements not yet attached to document (detached during SSR hydration), getComputedStyle returns empty string and fallback value isn't used, leading to transparent buttons.

Repro:
- On first paint, theme resolver runs in component constructor before mount and returns ''. Later, mount attaches elements but theme has been cached as '' and not recomputed.

Relevant code:

function resolveCssVar(el, varName, fallback) {
  const val = getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(varName);
  return val || fallback;
}

Fix:
- If getComputedStyle returns empty and el.isConnected === false, defer resolution until connected (use MutationObserver or run in useEffect after mount), or fallback to documentElement computed style.
- Add cache invalidation so that on mount the cached '' value is replaced.

Please implement deferred resolution and add unit + integration tests simulating detached elements during SSR hydration.

Long: CLI 'publish' command fails with ENOENT when package.json contains workspaces with missing packages

Scenario:
When running yarn publish through our CLI helper, it fails with ENOENT trying to read a workspace package that was removed but still listed in package.json workspaces array. The helper doesn't validate workspace paths and crashes.

Stack trace:

Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/repo/packages/missing/package.json'
    at Object.openSync (fs.js:xxx)
    at readPackage (/lib/cli/publish.js:45:18)

Desired behavior:
- Validate workspaces and ignore missing ones with a warning instead of throwing
- Provide a --strict flag to fail on missing workspace if user desires stricter behavior

Please update publish flow to catch ENOENT and continue. Add a log message listing missing workspace paths and add integration tests with a mock filesystem where some workspace entries are absent.

Long: The API uses multiple HTTP clients with inconsistent error handling. Example stack:

UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9200
    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect [as oncomplete] (node:net:1157:16)

Provide TypeScript interface:

interface HttpClient { get<T>(url: string, opts?: Options): Promise<T>; post<T>(url: string, body: any): Promise<T>; }

Long: After enabling ts-node/register for local dev, the production build started failing with runtime errors due to mixing ESM and CommonJS. Error:

Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /srv/api/dist/controllers/user.controller.js

Long: The API's type definitions for third-party webhook payloads are missing, causing runtime errors. Example failing test:

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'customerId')
    at WebhookHandler.handle (/src/webhooks/stripe.ts:22:15)

Current code expects req.body as any. Please:

- Validate incoming webhook signatures and parse JSON body to typed event

Long: The API has inconsistent promise rejection handling in Express routes. Example error logged:

UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '/var/log/app.log'
    at Object.openSync (fs.js:...) 

This stems from async route handlers not being wrapped and Express not catching rejected promises. Current patterns:

app.get('/users', async (req, res) => { const users = await userService.list(); res.json(users); });

If userService.list throws, the error isn't passed to next(). Refactor to add an asyncWrapper(fn) that returns (req,res,next) => Promise.resolve(fn(req,res,next)).catch(next) and apply to all routes (or use a library). Provide TypeScript definition for asyncWrapper and update router files.

Long: Intermittent startup crash when CONFIG_ENCRYPTED=true. Error below. The microservice expects a plain text config but sometimes receives base64 encrypted JSON from our secrets manager. We need to support auto-detection and decryption.

Error log:

Error: Unexpected token � in JSON at position 0
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at Object.loadConfig (/app/src/config/index.js:88:22)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:93:5)

Reproduction steps:
1) Set CONFIG_ENCRYPTED=true and CONFIG_DATA to base64 of encrypted payload.
2) Start container; crash occurs because loader tries JSON.parse before decrypting.

Desired behavior:
- If CONFIG_ENCRYPTED=true: decode base64, decrypt with AES256 using DECRYPTION_KEY env var, then parse JSON.
- If decryption fails, log clear error with masked key info and exit gracefully.

Example decryption flow (pseudo-js):
const encrypted = Buffer.from(process.env.CONFIG_DATA, 'base64');
const key = process.env.DECRYPTION_KEY; // must be set
const decipher = crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', keyBuf, iv);
let decrypted = Buffer.concat([decipher.update(encrypted), decipher.final()]);
const config = JSON.parse(decrypted.toString('utf8'));

Please add unit tests, integration test in CI, and detailed startup logs.

Change the default JSON serializer from Jackson to Gson in the SDK configuration; expose a Serializer interface so users can plug their own.
Expose request and response headers on ApiResponse object — currently only body and status code are available.
Make ApiClient thread-safe and document it: synchronize internal HttpClient initialization to avoid race conditions during lazy init.
Remove limit of 50 results in ListResourcesResponse; instead support server-side pagination tokens with ListResourcesRequest.nextPageToken.
Add bulkCreate(List<Entity>) endpoint to the SDK that performs batch requests with configurable batchSize and parallelism.
Add support for retries with exponential backoff and jitter in the default transport layer; allow users to configure RetryPolicy.

Add a @Beta annotation to experimental APIs and update the release notes; include instructions for stability guarantees.

Support service discovery via environment variable SERVICE_URL and add priority: explicit config > env var > default host.

Add automatic gzip compression of request bodies when payload > 1MB; provide opt-out via client config.
Expose metrics (request count, success/failure, latency) via Micrometer integration; add PrometheusMeterRegistry example.
Add helper method ApiClient.downloadTo(Path) to stream responses to disk without buffering entire body in memory.
Add an isHealthy() method to ApiClient that performs a lightweight health check endpoint call and caches results for 5s.
Update WebSocket handler to deliver messages via a Flow.Publisher<String> so reactive clients can subscribe easily.
Support adding interceptors that can mutate outgoing requests and incoming responses; provide sample logging interceptor.

Introduce a PaginationIterable<T> that lazily fetches pages for list operations instead of returning full lists.
Add native support for JSON Patch (RFC 6902) via applyPatch(Entity, JsonNode) utility and server-side compatibility notes.
Make all model classes immutable: replace setters with builders and mark fields final to improve thread safety.
Add an option to use HTTP/2 for transports when available; include negotiation and fallback logic to HTTP/1.1.
Expose a method setProxy(Proxy) on ClientConfig to allow SDK users behind corporate proxies to configure proxy settings.

Add transaction support to DB-backed SDK methods: beginTransaction(), commit(), rollback() with clear concurrency docs.

Support streaming large responses as InputStream and provide transfer progress callbacks to avoid OutOfMemoryErrors.
Add method ApiClient.shutdownGracefully(Duration) to allow pending requests to complete before closing resources.
Refactor SDK to use generic Response<T> so typed responses avoid casting and unsafe unchecked warnings.

Add new method watchResources(WatchOptions) that returns a reactive Flux<ResourceChange> for realtime updates.
Make SDK compatible with Android by shading java.desktop and excluding unsupported classes; add CI target for Android 8+.
Fix memory leak: HttpResponse bodies are not closed on non-200 responses; ensure InputStreams are closed in finally blocks.
Add circuit breaker support (resilience4j) with default thresholds and allow users to override via ClientConfig.
Change default JSON field naming to snake_case to align with server; expose mapper config toggle for backward compat.

Long-running: The SDK's paginated list calls are returning all pages synchronously, causing timeouts for high-volume endpoints. Repro steps:
1) Call client.listAllResources() for tenant with ~50k resources
2) SDK attempts to fetch all pages in one thread and aggregates into ArrayList
3) JVM runs out of heap and process OOMs

Stack trace snippet:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
    at java.util.Arrays.copyOf(Arrays.java:3332)
    at java.util.ArrayList.grow(ArrayList.java:237)
    at java.util.ArrayList.add(ArrayList.java:459)

Request: Provide a streaming iterable and a sample using Iterator<Resource> that fetches pages on demand; also add a maxResults limit option.

Long: After upgrade, clients get ClassCastException in response parsing for generics. Error log:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ClassCastException: java.util.LinkedHashMap cannot be cast to com.example.sdk.model.User
    at com.example.sdk.internal.ResponseParser.parse(ResponseParser.java:74)

Example code causing issue:

The parser uses TypeReference without proper generic type capture. Request: Fix ResponseParser to accept TypeReference<T> and use mapper.readValue(bytes, new TypeReference<T>() {}) pattern so List<User> and Map<String, User> deserialize correctly. Add regression test for List<User> parsing.

Long: Need to add idempotency key support for POST operations. Situation: When the network retries a POST, duplicate resources are created. Proposal:
- Add Request.withIdempotencyKey(String) method
- Send X-Idempotency-Key header on applicable requests
- Server returns 409 with existing resource location if duplicate

Example usage:
CreateRequest req = new CreateRequest(...).withIdempotencyKey(UUID.randomUUID().toString());
CreateResponse resp = client.create(req);

Also update docs and add sample showing how to recover on 409 by using returned resource id.

Long: The SDK currently swallows InterruptedException inside internal worker threads, causing thread interrupts to be ignored and preventing graceful shutdown. Repro steps:

3) Application doesn't terminate because worker threads don't respect interrupts

at java.lang.Thread.sleep(Native Method)
at com.example.sdk.poller.Poller.run(Poller.java:78)

Request: Propagate InterruptedException correctly (set Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and break loops), add shutdownGracefully(Duration) to ApiClient, and add unit tests that assert threads terminate on interrupt.

Long: Database-backed caching in SDK returns stale entries after update calls. Details:

- After client.update(resource), subsequent get(id) returns old cached value.

r.setName("new");
client.update(r);

Long: Support for multi-tenant header propagation is missing. Problem: SDK needs to send X-Tenant-Id on all outgoing calls. Proposed changes:

Client client = new Client(cfg);

Long: The SDK's builder pattern mixes required and optional properties inconsistently: some required fields are optional in builder and cause runtime errors. Example:

client.doSomething(); // fails with IllegalStateException: apiKey missing

Profile app startup time and reduce boot latency — investigate slow initializers and eager_load settings in config/application.rb.
Reduce app memory usage on low-end devices by optimizing image caching and downscaling before display.
Avoid N+1 queries in feed API: add appropriate includes for associations used in serializers.
Investigate slow push notification batching — batch DB queries and avoid serial ActiveRecord calls inside loops.
Move heavy JSON serialization to background jobs for large export endpoints to avoid request timeouts.
Cache user preference lookups (current_user.settings) with Rails.cache.fetch to reduce DB hits during navigation.
Refactor image-heavy feed to use pagination and lazy-loading to cut down initial payload size.
Switch expensive Ruby loops in controller to use ActiveRecord calculations (sum/avg) to reduce Ruby-level iteration.
Use Rack::Deflater for API responses to reduce bandwidth; ensure mobile clients can accept gzip.
Limit included associations in serializers to required fields only to reduce memory allocation for API responses.
Optimize DB by adding missing indexes for frequent query filters like user_id, created_at, and status.
Reduce GC pressure by reusing objects in hot loops (avoid allocating new arrays/hashes repeatedly).

Convert blocking file I/O in controller to background processing (ActiveStorage direct uploads) to improve responsiveness.
Use HTTP/2 multiplexing on API host to reduce latency for multiple concurrent asset requests.
Move static asset serving to CDN and set far-future Cache-Control for packaged JS/CSS assets.
Bundle and minify frontend Ruby templates and remove unused helper methods to speed up view rendering.
Investigate slow sign-up flow: remove synchronous email validation callouts and batch external API requests.

Short: Add fragment caching for header/user badge partials.

Short: Memoize computed heavy methods on models (e.g., expensive_profile_score).
Short: Use find_each for bulk user processing to avoid loading all records into memory.
Short: Increase ActiveRecord connection pool in production to match Puma threads.
Short: Remove deep_dup calls in serializers; avoid duplicating large hashes.
Short: Move image resizing to server-side worker and return CDN URLs only.
Short: Compress PNG/JPEG assets offline and serve optimized images.
Short: Replace to_json on AR collections with jbuilder templates to stream JSON.
Short: Remove stringify_keys! in hot paths that mutate shared hashes.

Medium: The feed API is timing out for users with many follows. When loading posts we perform multiple separate queries for likes, comments count, and author profile. Can we consolidate into a single ActiveRecord query with joins/includes and use select('COUNT(...) AS ...') for counts? Also consider caching counts in a counter cache column.

Medium: On Android devices the app feels sluggish when rendering the timeline — the backend response size for /v1/timeline is huge (full post bodies, nested comments, author avatars). Please create a slimmed-down API payload for mobile clients and add a flag param like ?view=minimal to reduce JSON size.

Medium: The avatar upload endpoint spikes memory and CPU: we process image variants in-line and create multiple Tempfiles per upload. Move image processing to Sidekiq workers, use direct S3 uploads from mobile app, and ensure ActiveStorage uses variants lazily.

Medium: We're experiencing many DB deadlocks during concurrent follow/unfollow actions. The service currently updates counters by reading then writing. Use atomic counter updates (increment_counter/decrement_counter) and wrap in transactions with consistent ordering to avoid lock contention.

Medium: Login latency is high because of synchronous LDAP and 3rd-party verification. Add local caching (memcached) for LDAP results with short TTL and fall back to async verification for non-critical checks.

Medium: The background job queue is backlogged. Jobs performing large AR find + update loops are causing long GC pauses. Switch to batching with find_in_batches, reduce per-job memory, and tune Sidekiq concurrency and lifecycle hooks.

Medium: API JSON serialization uses active_model_serializers and is slow for large collections. Consider using fast_jsonapi or GitHub's jsonapi-serializer and benchmark. Also add streaming (ActionController::Live or Rack hijack) for large exports.

Medium: Excessive rendering time from nested partials in Messages view. Convert deeply nested partials into presenter objects or build HTML on client side. Profile with rack-mini-profiler to find hot templates.
Medium: We see many TCP connection timeouts for asset host in certain regions. Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for CDN fetches and pre-warm CDN caches for popular assets.
Medium: Mobile app reports inconsistent list scroll performance; server sends large arrays of small items. Implement server-side pagination with cursor tokens and limit default page size to 20.
Medium: Several endpoints frequently query Redis for feature flags per request. Introduce local in-process LRU cache (with TTL) for hot flags to reduce Redis roundtrips.
Medium: The session store uses DB-backed sessions causing high latency. Migrate to Redis session store or signed cookies to reduce DB IO under spike traffic.

Long: Rails app experiencing severe GC pauses under load when processing image-heavy feeds. Example GC log fragment:

[I, [2025-10-12T14:23:10.123456 #12345]]  INFO -- : CPU time: user 0.52s, system 0.03s
[I, [2025-10-12T14:23:10.123789 #12345]]  INFO -- : GC: 12345.6ms (full) 56789 -> 34567 -> 20000 MB, 98.12% free

Repro steps:

2) Call GET /v1/timeline concurrently (50 requests).
3) Observe worker memory growth and long GC pauses.

Code snippet where Tempfiles are created:

def process_upload(io)
  img = MiniMagick::Image.read(io.read)
  variants.each do |size|
    t = Tempfile.new(['variant', '.jpg'])
    img.resize(size)
    img.write(t.path)
    UploadWorker.perform_async(t.path)
  end
end

Request: Move image processing out of request thread, stream uploads to S3, reuse buffers, and avoid reading entire IO into memory (use IO.copy_stream or stream processing). Consider using ImageProcessing gem with shrinking and streaming support.

Long: Intermittent PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server when under spike load. Stack trace:

ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished (PG::ConnectionBad: could not connect to server: Connection timed out\n\tIs the server running on host "db-prod" (10.0.0.15) and accepting TCP/IP connections on port 5432?)\nfrom /app/vendor/bundle/ruby/3.0.0/gems/pg-1.2.3/lib/pg.rb:56:in `connect'

Logs show pool exhaustion and long waiting for checkout: "ActiveRecord::ConnectionTimeoutError: could not obtain a database connection within 5.000 seconds"

Current config: Puma threads 16, workers 4; database.yml pool: 5. Need to align connection pool with Puma threads/workers and increase pool or reduce threads. Also audit queries that open connections without releasing or long transactions. Suggested changes:
- Set ENV DATABASE_POOL = (PUMA_THREADS * PUMA_WORKERS) + buffer
- Ensure Sidekiq processes have separate DB pools
- Add instrumentation to log connection checkout times

Long: Users report slow search API with long-running SQL and high latency. Example slow query log:

# Slow Query: 6.72s
SELECT posts.* FROM "posts" WHERE (LOWER(title) LIKE '%rails%') ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50 OFFSET 0;

We currently do ILIKE '%term%' searches causing full table scan. Proposal:
- Add tsvector column and GIN index for full-text search on title and body:
  add_column :posts, :search_vector, :tsvector
  add_index :posts, :search_vector, using: :gin
- Populate via trigger or background migration and use plainto_tsquery/@@ for search.
- Example replacement SQL:
  SELECT * FROM posts WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'rails') ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50;

Also consider using ElasticSearch/OpenSearch for advanced ranking and offloading load from primary DB.

Long: Crash in JSON parsing under heavy load causing OOM and slow response times. Error:

NoMemoryError: failed to allocate memory
  from /usr/local/lib/ruby/3.0.0/json/common.rb:216:in `parse'

Controller code:

def import
  data = JSON.parse(request.body.read)
  data['items'].each do |i|
    Item.create!(i)
  end
end

This reads entire request body and parses huge JSON into memory. Repro steps:
- POST a JSON array of ~10k items (~200MB) to /v1/import
- Observe worker memory spikes and crash

Fixes: use streaming JSON parser (Oj with :handler or yajl), validate content-length and limit size, process in chunks, or accept NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) and stream-parsed objects into the DB with find_in_batches to reduce memory footprint.

Long: High 95th percentile latency on /v1/profile due to N+1 and expensive view rendering. Example stack trace from Skylight showing hotspots:

app/views/profiles/show.html.erb:27 - render @posts
app/models/post.rb:103 - comments_count

Current code:

def show
  @user = User.find_by(username: params[:username])
  @posts = @user.posts.order(created_at: :desc).limit(50)
end

In view:
<% @posts.each do |post| %>
  <%= render 'post', post: post %>
<% end %>

Partial accesses post.comments.count and post.author.avatar_url causing N+1s.

Suggested changes:
- Eager load associations: @posts = @user.posts.includes(:comments, :author)
- Add comments_count counter_cache on posts to avoid count queries
- Consider using a dedicated query with joins to fetch necessary fields only:
  Post.where(user_id: @user.id).select('posts.id, posts.body, posts.comments_count, users.avatar_url').joins(:author)
- Add fragment caching for post partials keyed by post.cache_key and current_user permissions.

Long: Sidekiq workers are getting killed with SIGKILL, memory spikes before death. System log excerpt:

Oct 12 17:02:33 app-sidekiq[2222]: [Worker#12] performing Class#perform_async(123)
Oct 12 17:02:35 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2222 (sidekiq) score 946 or sacrifice child
Oct 12 17:02:36 systemd[1]: sidekiq.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL

Job code:

class ProcessFeedWorker
  include Sidekiq::Worker

  def perform(user_id)
    user = User.find(user_id)
    posts = user.following_posts.includes(:author, :likes)
    posts.each do |p|
      heavy_proc(p)
    end
  end

  def heavy_proc(post)
    # generates many objects, reads images, etc.
  end
end

Action items:
- Break large jobs into smaller jobs with batch processing
- Limit preloading to only required fields
- Use Sidekiq unique jobs or batching to avoid duplicate work
- Instrument memory usage and use sidekiq-limit_fetch or throttling

Long: API returns intermittent 500 on high concurrency. Traceback in logs:

NoMethodError (undefined method `[]' for nil:NilClass):
  app/controllers/api/v1/notifications_controller.rb:58:in `block in index'
  app/controllers/api/v1/notifications_controller.rb:45:in `map'

Controller code:

def index
  notifications = current_user.notifications.order(created_at: :desc).limit(100)
  render json: notifications.map { |n| render_notification(n) }
end

def render_notification(n)
  { id: n.id, actor: n.actor['username'], text: n.payload['message'] }
end

Error occurs because some notification.payloads are nil due to older migration. Under concurrent requests some rows are lazily loaded and payload is nil. But main perf problem is allocation of huge array for 100 notifications and heavy mapping.

Fix:
- Sanitize nil payloads and use safe navigation: n.payload&.[]('message')
- Use as_json on AR collection with serializer that streams
- Add DB migration to backfill missing payloads
- Consider returning paginated, minimal notification representations and load details on demand

Long: Mobile app reports slow login for users with many devices; we iterate all devices to revoke tokens. Example code:

def revoke_all_tokens_for(user)
  user.devices.each do |d|
    d.tokens.each { |t| t.revoke! }
  end
end

When a user has 5k devices this blocks request and spikes memory. Stack trace in logs:

app/services/token_service.rb:23:in `revoke_all_tokens_for'

Recommendations:
- Use batch SQL to update tokens: Token.where(device_id: user.devices.select(:id)).update_all(revoked: true)
- Avoid loading associations into memory
- Use background job to handle mass revokes and return immediate response to user
- Add index on tokens.device_id for update performance

Long: High latency in GraphQL endpoint: resolvers firing N+1 queries. Example schema resolver:

field :posts, [PostType], null: false

def posts
  Post.order(created_at: :desc).limit(50)
end

In PostType we resolve comments_count and author. GraphQL adds per-field fetches. Logs show 200 additional queries per page.

Proposed fixes:
- Use dataloader pattern (BatchLoader gem) or graphql-batch to batch DB calls
- Preload associations in root resolver if possible: Post.includes(:author, :comments)
- Use counter_cache for counts to avoid counting queries

Code example using BatchLoader:

field :author, AuthorType, null: false

def author
  BatchLoader.for(object.author_id).batch(default_value: nil) do |author_ids, loader|
    Author.where(id: author_ids).each { |a| loader.call(a.id, a) }
  end
end

Long: We're leaking memory in controller due to per-request class variable growth. Listen from production memory profiler shows retained objects: strings from building file paths.

Example problematic code:

class AttachmentController < ApplicationController
  @@cache = {}

  def download
    key = params[:key]
    @@cache[key] ||= build_path_for(key)
    send_file @@cache[key]
  end
end

When many unique keys are requested @@cache grows unbounded. Fix by using LRU cache with bounded size (lru_redux or ActiveSupport::Cache::MemoryStore with size limit), or avoid caching paths in global variable. Also ensure temp file cleanup. Add metrics for cache size and eviction.

Long: API reports serialization slowdown due to repeated use of to_json on large nested ActiveRecord objects leading to deep object graph traversal. Example code:

def export
  users = User.includes(:posts => [:comments, :likes]).where(active: true)
  render json: users.to_json
end

This creates huge JSON in memory and blocks. Propose streaming CSV export with enumerator or use Oj.dump with mode: :compat and use incremental dumping. Example streaming response:

self.response_body = Enumerator.new do |y|
  User.find_each(batch_size: 1000) do |user|
    y << user.to_json
  end
end

Also avoid includes that load unneeded relations; select only required fields for export.

Long: Frequent ActionController::RoutingError for asset pipeline causing slow 404 handling and logs flooding. Example production log shows repeated mime-type negotiation and Rails middleware stack overhead. We currently serve assets through Rails in production. Change to have nginx/CDN serve static assets and set config.public_file_server.enabled = ENV['RAILS_SERVE_STATIC_FILES']. Present code in production.rb:

config.public_file_server.enabled = ENV['RAILS_SERVE_STATIC_FILES'].present?

But we have ENV false. Fix deployment to enable static file serving to webserver and configure CDN edge caching. Also set config.assets.compile = false to avoid on-the-fly compilation.

Long: Mobile app complaining about inconsistent timestamps causing re-render thrashing due to serialization of times with timezone conversions. Heavy usage of Time.zone.parse in controllers is expensive. Example hot code:

params['events'].each do |e|
  e['time'] = Time.zone.parse(e['time'])
  Event.create!(e)
end

Parsing thousands of times becomes slow. Optimize by avoiding Ruby parsing in bulk — accept epoch integers from client or parse in C-extension (use Time.at) if possible. Also consider using ActiveRecord's built-in time casting via insert of integer seconds and let DB handle conversion. Add benchmarks comparing Time.iso8601 vs Time.parse vs Time.at.

Long: Debugging a production slowdown: CPU profiling shows a lot of time spent in GC and String allocations due to repeated string concatenation building SQL fragments. Example code:

scope = "SELECT * FROM posts WHERE " + "user_id = #{user.id}"
scope += " AND status = '#{status}'" if status
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute(scope)

This spawns many temporary strings. Use parameterized queries and ARel where clauses to minimize allocations:

posts = Post.where(user_id: user.id)
posts = posts.where(status: status) if status.present?
posts.to_a

Also reduce use of string interpolation in hot paths, use << on a pre-allocated String when building large logs, or use sprintf to reduce temporary objects.

Long: App uses global Mutex around profile updates causing contention and slow concurrent requests. Example snippet:

PROFILE_LOCK = Mutex.new

def update_profile(user_id, attrs)
  PROFILE_LOCK.synchronize do
    u = User.find(user_id)
    u.update!(attrs)
  end
end

This serializes updates for all users. We need to limit lock scope to per-user (use Redis-based per-key locks like redlock or use row-level database locking with SELECT FOR UPDATE within transaction). Prefer optimistic locking if suitable (lock_version) to reduce contention. Also add metrics for lock wait times.

Long: We need to optimize push notification batching when sending to APNs/FCM. Current code sends one HTTP request per device, which is slow and prone to rate limits. Example code:

devices.each do |d|
  Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port) do |http|
    req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
    req.body = payload.to_json
    http.request(req)
  end
end

Switch to provider bulk APIs, maintain persistent connections, and use concurrent requests in threads/pools. Use HTTP/2 multiplexing for APNs. Also throttle and retry with exponential backoff for 5xx errors. Consider grouping messages and using provider SDKs for efficient batching.

Long: High object allocation in controller due to using HashWithIndifferentAccess repeatedly; performance profiler points to deep symbol/string conversion. Example code:

params = HashWithIndifferentAccess.new(request.params)
process(params)

This is unnecessary — use params directly (already a HashWithIndifferentAccess) or permit only required fields with strong parameters. Avoid converting large nested payloads into new HashWithIndifferentAccess. For better perf, use simple Hash and string keys when iterating heavily.

Long: Fix slow mobile image gallery loading: server-side returns full-resolution images for thumbnails causing high bandwidth and latency. Example log shows transfer of 5MB per image. Current controller:

def show_gallery
  images = user.images.limit(100)
  render json: images.map { |i| { url: i.file.service_url } }
end

Instead, store/serve low-res thumbnails via ActiveStorage variants and ensure URLs point to small variants. Example:

images.map { |i| { thumb_url: rails_blob_representation_url(i.file.variant(resize_to_limit: [200,200])) } }

Also add client-side caching headers and Cache-Control max-age.

Long: Investigate high latency when fetching user feed from microservice aggregator. Network logs show many small HTTP calls to profile, media, and reactions services. Example trace:

-> /aggregator/fetch (main request)
  -> GET /profiles/:id (120ms)
  -> GET /media/ids (210ms)
  -> GET /reactions?post_ids[]=1&post_ids[]=2... (310ms)
Total: >700ms

We should reduce round trips by consolidating calls in aggregator service into a single bulk endpoint, use HTTP/2 where possible, and parallelize independent calls. Also add caching layer for profile data (TTL 5 minutes), and use combiners on client-side to prefetch data when idle.

Long: We are hitting ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid due to long IN lists when fetching reactions for many posts in feed. Error:

ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid (PG::TooManyParameters: ERROR:  bind message supplies 65537 parameters, but prepared statement "" requires 65536)

Code creating query:

post_ids = posts.map(&:id)
Reaction.where(post_id: post_ids, user_id: current_user.id)

When post_ids count grows large (>60k) the parameter list exceeds DB limits. Fix by chunking queries with find_in_batches or use temporary table approach: create a temp table of post_ids and join, or use JSONB parameter to pass array and use WHERE post_id = ANY($1) with a single array parameter (and bind as PG::TextEncoder::Array). Also guard feed size to reasonable limit.

Long: The app's encryption/decryption routines for sensitive fields are CPU-heavy causing slow signup. Example code uses OpenSSL::Cipher in Ruby for each field per request:

cipher = OpenSSL::Cipher.new('aes-256-gcm')
cipher.encrypt
cipher.key = key
cipher.iv = iv
encrypted = cipher.update(plain) + cipher.final

This is invoked multiple times. Offload to a background job for non-critical fields, or use per-column transparent encryption using database-level support (PG crypto extension). Alternatively, use a C-extension or native library wrapper that reuses Cipher instances in a pool to avoid constant initialization costs. Add benchmarks for Cipher.new overhead.

Long: API rate limiter implemented with per-request Redis INCR is causing hot key contention and latency. We have code:

count = $redis.incr(key)
$redis.expire(key, 60) unless $redis.ttl(key) > 0

Under burst traffic the TTL check causes multiple instructions and race. Replace with a single Lua script to atomic INCR and EXPIRE, or use Redis' INCR with EXPIRE using SET key 1 EX NX for initial set. Also consider using token bucket algorithm in Redis or Leaky bucket in-memory token buckets for low-latency local rate limiting per server.

Long: We should optimize database schema for message search — current design stores searchable message text in messages.body (text) and we run LIKE queries. Slow query example:

SELECT * FROM messages WHERE body ILIKE '%urgent%'

Proposed schema changes:
- Add a generated tsvector column: ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN body_tsv tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('english', coalesce(body, ''))) STORED;
- Add GIN index: CREATE INDEX idx_messages_body_tsv ON messages USING gin(body_tsv);
- Update queries: WHERE body_tsv @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'urgent')

Plan a backfill job to populate tsvector for existing rows and include migration steps. This will massively reduce CPU and IO for search on mobile queries.

Long: Investigate slow Redis response times for session store causing request queuing. Example REDIS slowlog entries show many commands > 100ms. We're storing large session blobs (~20KB) per user leading to heavy serialization overhead with Marshal.dump. Code:

Rails.application.config.session_store :redis_store, servers: ENV['REDIS_URL'], expire_after: 14.days

Optimizations:
- Reduce session size to minimal (store only session id and small token), move profile/state to separate cache keyed by user
- Switch serialization to JSON (faster in some cases) or use msgpack for compactness
- Increase redis resources or use sharded redis for sessions
- Add instrumentation for average session read/write sizes and latency
Add a migration helper to detect unapplied migrations and return a list of pending migration file names.
Rename migration files to include timestamp prefixes using the library's naming convention (yyyyMMddHHmmss_) and update the migrator to parse them.
Support running migrations concurrently-safe so multiple processes don't apply the same migration at once.
Expose a function migrate.rollback(steps: usize) to undo the last N migrations.
Add CLI flag --dry-run for the zig-migrate binary to print SQL statements without executing them.
Improve error messages when migration SQL fails to include the failing SQL and line number.
Add support for transactionless migrations for DDL that can't run inside transactions (Postgres specific).
Add an option to verify migration checksums on startup and fail if local migration files don't match recorded checksums in migration history table.
Integrate environment-variable based DB URLs (ZIG_DB_URL) and document precedence between CLI args and env vars.
Add support for MySQL in addition to Postgres — implement connection pool abstraction and SQL dialect adapter.
Make migrator gracefully handle 'already_exists' errors so idempotent create statements don't abort entire migration.
Add a migration test harness that runs each migration against an in-memory or ephemeral DB and reports failures.
Document the recommended naming scheme and file format for Zig migration scripts in the README.
Add SQL templating support: allow migrations to be Zig scripts that compile and emit SQL with safety checks.
Expose migration status via HTTP for a small admin API endpoint to show current version and pending count.
Fix bug: migrator fails when migration directory contains non-.sql files (e.g., .DS_Store). Should ignore unknown files.
Allow custom migration table name via MigratorConfig.migrations_table_name field.
Add option to skip verification of checksum when running in CI to speed up test runs.
Support applying only a named subset of migrations (labels/tags) instead of chronological order.
Add tracing spans around each migration step using zig-trace (or custom tracer interface) to measure long-running migrations.
Return a typed MigrationResult instead of bool so caller can inspect applied, skipped, and failed migrations.
Add migration fixture utilities for tests: create_temp_db(), apply_migrations(), teardown().
Improve logging: include migration duration in ms and query count when running a script.
Add ability to set a pre- and post-migration callback (fn(context: MigrationContext) void) to run validation or cleanup.
Support parameterized SQL migrations: pass runtime parameters (e.g., tenant_id) safely without string concat.
Fix: When running multiple migrations in one transaction, an SQL error causes the transaction rollback but migrator still marks later migrations as applied. Ensure atomicity.
Add option to compress/pack migrations into a single binary asset for deployment and add loader to apply those migrations.
Add better Windows path normalization for migration discovery (handle backslashes and case-insensitivity).
Add support for SQL migration 'up' and 'down' within the same file separated by -- up / -- down markers.
Add a convenience macro to embed migration SQL in Zig source (pub const migrations = embedFile("migrations.sql");) and index them.
When migration fails, print full stack trace with Zig allocator debug info and line numbers to help debugging.
Add integration with docker-compose test runner: start ephemeral Postgres, run migrations, and run test suite.
Improve schema locking: create advisory locking via Postgres pg_advisory_lock to prevent concurrent migration runs.
Add API: migrator.getCurrentVersion() -> u64 and migrator.getPendingMigrations() -> []MigrationMetadata.
Support schema-qualified migrations (schema name prefix) and migrate per-schema in multi-tenant Postgres setups.
Add safety check before applying destructive changes: require a special flag --confirm-destructive to run ALTER DROP COLUMN statements.
Bug: Zig migration runner panics with 'out of bounds' when migration file is exactly 4096 bytes — investigate buffer handling.
Add unit tests around filename ordering — ensure lexicographic vs timestamp sorting works as intended for mixed names.
Expose connection pool config to migrator so large migrations can increase pool size temporarily.
Add migration plan generation: compute SQL that will run and how schema will change (columns added/removed) and print a plan.
Add support to import legacy Ruby/ActiveRecord migration table entries and convert them to Zig library migration records.
Add example in README showing embedding migrations, configuring migrations table, and running from a binary.
Add TypeScript frontend example that fetches migration status via admin API and displays progress bar while migrations run.
Add ability to run migrations per-tenant from an HTTP admin request with rate-limiting and concurrency control.

Medium: Tests failing intermittently in CI: applying migrations against ephemeral Postgres sometimes times out after 30s. The stack shows the goroutine waiting on a connection. We should add configurable timeouts and better retry logic in connection acquisition. Example config: MigratorConfig { connect_timeout_ms = 60000, retry_backoff_ms = 200 }.

Medium: When running migrations in Docker, the library can't find migrations when path includes symlinks. On Linux symlinked path returns different inode order causing inconsistent sorting. Need to normalize resolved paths via fs.realPath() before scanning.

Medium: The API currently returns []u8 for migration SQL content; this copies the whole file into memory. For very large migrations (>50MB) we should stream the SQL and execute chunk-by-chunk to reduce memory usage. Propose adding Migrator.executeStream(istream: any) -> error.

Medium: Add support for automatic retries on serialization errors (Postgres error code 40001) when running long transactional migrations. Should retry with exponential backoff up to configured attempts.

Medium: The migrator's error type is an opaque error set. For better library interop, create an exported error set MigrationError with variants: IOError, SQLExecutionError{code, message}, ChecksumMismatch, LockTimeout, etc.
Medium: Provide a clear rollback strategy for failed partial migrations: either fully rollback transactionally or mark migration as failed in table and provide CLI to resume or revert.
Medium: Add support for migration grouping: group multiple .sql files into a batch to run in a single transaction. Useful for logically related changes.
Medium: Add options for migration file encoding detection (UTF-8 with BOM). Currently migrations with BOM fail to parse; strip BOM before execution.
Medium: Add a dev-mode that automatically runs pending migrations on program start but only when ENVIRONMENT=development, with optional safety prompts.
Medium: Allow customizing SQL dialects by providing a Dialect trait: escape_identifier, placeholder_for_param(index), supports_transactions_for_ddl, etc. Provide Postgres and MySQL implementations.
Medium: Improve documentation of migration table schema: include SQL to create migrations table and expected columns: id, name, checksum, applied_at, duration_ms.
Medium: Add inspect command to the CLI that shows per-migration checksums and marks mismatches with a warning rather than failing.

Long: After upgrading Zig to 0.10.0, migrations fail with ConnectionError and stack trace shows TLS handshake failure when connecting to cloud Postgres. Repro:

zig build run --target x86_64-linux -- migrate --db "postgres://user:pass@db.example.com:5432/app"

Error output:

Error: ConnectionError
    at connect (src/db/conn.zig:87)
    at std.process.main (src/main.zig:23)
Caused by: TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate

Our deployment uses a custom CA certificate that's available on disk at /etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem. Previously, the migrator honored PGSSLROOTCERT env var but after recent changes it no longer does. Please reintroduce env var support and allow setting custom CA via MigratorConfig.tls_root_cert_path: ?[]const u8. Add tests mocking TLS failure and verify proper env passthrough. Example config snippet:

const cfg = MigratorConfig{
    .database_url = "postgres://...",
    .tls_root_cert_path = std.fs.path.bufAlloc(&allocator, "/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem") catch null,
};

Also update README to document SSL options and mention Zig version compatibility notes.

Long: Encountering migration lock timeouts when running multiple migrators concurrently in production. Logs below:

2025-10-19T12:00:01Z INFO Attempting to acquire migration lock
2025-10-19T12:00:11Z ERROR Failed to acquire migration lock: timeout after 10s
Error: LockTimeout
    at migrator.acquireLock (src/migrator/lock.zig:42)
    at migrator.run (src/migrator/main.zig:128)

We use a naive 'select for update' lock and it isn't robust. Proposed fix: use Postgres advisory locks (pg_try_advisory_lock) with configurable lock_key derived from db name + migrations table name. Add backoff and jitter to retries; optional deadlock detection logging. Example SQL to acquire lock: SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtext('mydb:migrations'));

Also propose exposing MigratorConfig.lock_timeout_ms and lock_retry_ms, and adding a CLI flag --lock-timeout. Add tests that spawn two migrators and assert only one acquires lock and other waits and exits gracefully or retries. Please include code snippet for lock acquisition in Zig:

const stmt = try conn.execAlloc("SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock($1)", &[hash]);
if (stmt.rows.len > 0 and stmt.rows[0][0] == "t") { // got lock }

Add clear docs about lock semantics and guarantee that the library will not mark migrations as applied if lock can't be obtained.

Long: Add verbose SQL logging with masked credentials. When connecting to DB we log the full connection string for debugging, which leaks passwords in CI logs. Example snippet from logs:

Connecting to postgres://user:password@db.example.com:5432/app

Please change logging to mask sensitive parts. Implement fn maskDbUrl(url: []const u8) []u8 that replaces password with ****: postgres://user:****@db.example.com:5432/app. Also add option to disable logging of database URLs entirely via MigratorConfig.log_sensitive = false.

Include tests covering edge cases like URLs with special characters, percent-encoding, and missing passwords. Update README with security guidance and ensure default CLI --verbose does not print credentials.

Long: Migration rollback doesn't replay triggers that were dropped during failed migration. Repro steps and code:

1) Existing DB has a trigger trg_a on table t.
2) Migration 20250701_modify_t.sql drops trigger, alters table, then recreates trigger.
3) Migration fails during recreate; migrator rolls back transaction but the trigger remains dropped on the DB.

Log excerpt:

Applying migration 20250701_modify_t
Executing: DROP TRIGGER trg_a ON t;
Executing: ALTER TABLE t ALTER COLUMN x TYPE bigint;
Executing: CREATE TRIGGER trg_a ...
ERROR: syntax error at or near "CREATE"
Transaction rolled back by server.
Migration marked failed.

Investigation shows some statements executed outside transaction due to 'transaction: none' header for the migration. However the first statements were run before the non-transactional portion, leaving DB in inconsistent state. Proposed changes:

- Provide clear documentation and linter to detect mixed transactional and non-transactional statements in same file.
- Enforce header-based behavior: if transaction: none, treat entire file as non-transactional; if transactional, wrap everything.
- For mixed-case, fail lint and refuse to run.

Add Zig code snippet for lint:

fn lintMigration(m: []const u8) !void {
    const hasTransactionalOnlyTokens = ...; // detect 'CONCURRENTLY', 'VACUUM' etc.
    if (hasTransactionalOnlyTokens and header.transaction == .None) {
        return error.InvalidMigrationMix;
    }
}

Add tests and update README with best practices for triggers and non-transactional steps.

Long: Build failing in CI on macOS with 'undefined reference to pthread' when running migration tests that use threads for concurrency. Error log:

/usr/bin/ld: /tmp/zig-cache/o/test_runner.o: in function `Thread.run'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

The test harness spins up threads to run parallel migrations. We need to ensure build flags include -pthread and Zig's build.zig adds .linkLibC(true) or appropriate options. Proposed changes:

- Update build.zig to set exe.linker_args append -pthread on posix and add .linkSystemLibrary("pthread") where necessary.
- Add CI matrix entry to run macOS and Linux builds.
- Add fallback single-threaded test mode if pthread is not available. Example test switch:

const MAX_PARALLEL = if (osSupportsThreads()) 8 else 1;

Add documentation about platform requirements for concurrent migration modes.

Long: The migrator's CLI exits with code 0 on partial failure if a migration fails but some were applied. This makes CI think migrations succeeded. Example run:

$ zig-migrate apply
Applying 1/3: 20250101_init... OK
Applying 2/3: 20250102_bad... FAILED
Applying 3/3: 20250103_later... SKIPPED

Exit code: 0

We should change behavior: any failure should result in non-zero exit code. Provide option --continue-on-error for specialized workflows. Update Zig main() to return appropriate error sets and map to exit codes. Example main change:

pub fn main() anyerror!void {
    if (result.failed) return error.MigrationFailed;
}

Add unit tests for exit codes and update CLI docs.

Long: Add audit logging for migration operations to comply with compliance requirements. Requirements:
- Record who triggered migration (user, service account) via context
- Record host, git commit hash, migration names and durations
- Expose logs in JSON lines format and optionally push to syslog

Proposed schema for audit table:

CREATE TABLE migration_audit (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  migration_name text NOT NULL,
  started_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  finished_at timestamptz,
  status text NOT NULL,
  actor text,
  host text,
  git_commit text,
  details jsonb
);

Zig logging snippet:

var audit = AuditEntry{ .migration_name = name, .started_at = std.time.milliTimestamp(), .actor = cfg.actor };
try audit.insert(db);
try runMigration();
try audit.markDone(db, status);

Add CLI flag --actor to specify initiator and environment variable MIGRATOR_COMMIT to auto-detect current git commit. Add tests for audit insertion and schema migration to create audit table automatically when missing.
Add an option to switch between compact and verbose list views for command output (single-letter flags like -c / -v).
Make the CLI use adaptive column widths when printing tables so long filenames don't wrap mid-word in terminals.
Improve error messages: replace "Operation failed" with actionable guidance and an exit code mapping table in docs.
Add a --no-color flag and respect NO_COLOR env var so scripts can consume output reliably.
Enable clickable URLs in output when running in supported terminals (print OSC 8 hyperlinks).
Add keyboard shortcut hints for interactive mode: show '(q)uit, (r)efresh, (h)elp' in the prompt footer.
Support UTF-8 and wide characters in table rendering; right now multi-byte icons break column alignment.
When using --json output, ensure pretty-printing is optional (--pretty) and stable key ordering for tests.
Improve startup banner: hide by default and add --banner to show ASCII art for demos.
Show a progress bar for long-running tasks and allow toggling TTY vs non-TTY behavior automatically.
Add environment-aware logging levels: follow RUST_LOG-style env variable but C++ friendly (CLI_LOG).
Add a configuration file parser to set preferred theme (colors/verbosity) with priority: CLI > env > config.
Make help output paginated (pipe to $PAGER) when more than terminal height lines; respect -h --help always.
Provide a compact mode for prompts that reduces confirmation dialogs for scripted runs (--yes-for-all).
Allow customizing the timestamp format in logs and include timezone in verbose mode.
Fix inconsistent exit codes: map validation errors to 2, runtime exceptions to 3, and internal errors to 4.
Add ANSI color theme presets (solarized, gruvbox) and an easy switch --theme=solarized-dark.
Make interactive prompts cancelable with Ctrl+C without leaving the terminal in a broken state (restore tty).
Detect terminal width at runtime and reflow help text when window is resized; handle SIGWINCH.
Add clearer warnings when running with insufficient permissions and suggest sudo or chmod commands.
Improve tab-completion scripts for bash/zsh/fish and add generator for auto-install in install docs.
Localize messages: add support for loading translations from .mo/.po files and a --lang option.
On config validation failure, print the offending JSON/YAML fragment with line numbers to help user fix it.

LONG: Autocompletion script failing for fish due to quoting differences; debug logs and patch idea

Symptoms: typed 'mycli st<TAB>' doesn't complete to 'status' in fish, but works in bash.

fish completion script generated by `mycli --completion=fish` looks like:

complete -c mycli -n '__fish_seen_subcommand_from' -a 'status' -d 'Show status'

But fish expects:

complete -c mycli -n "__fish_use_subcommand" -a "status" -d "Show status"

Also our generator emits unescaped single quotes which break when descriptions include apostrophes.

Repro:
1) Add command with description: "Show user's status"
2) Generate fish completion and source it
3) Try completion

Suggested fix: change generator to use fish-safe quoting (double quotes and escape inside) and use proper condition functions. Add unit tests generating completion for bash/zsh/fish and parse them with shellcheck where possible.

LONG: Crash when handling multi-threaded logging with spdlog + colors; stack trace and reproduction

We get a race leading to exception:
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  Cannot format message: logger already destroyed

Repro:
1) Run `mycli serve` which spawns worker threads
2) Send SIGTERM to stop the process while workers are still emitting logs

Backtrace (gdb):
#0  0x00007ffff7a1d428 in raise ()
#1  0x00007ffff7a1f02a in abort ()
#2  0x000055555555b3d6 in logging_thread_func() at src/logging.cpp:75
#3  0x00007ffff7bcf6db in start_thread ()

We call spdlog::drop_all() during shutdown but threads may still be logging. UX: ensure graceful shutdown sequence: signal workers to stop, join threads, then drop loggers. Consider using a shared_ptr logger and thread-safe sink or RCU-like lifetime. Also add a flag to run without colors in headless CI to avoid terminal-specific sinks causing issues.

LONG: Inconsistent handling of config paths on Windows vs POSIX leading to confusing UX; include code and sample paths

Issue: On Windows, config path is C:\Users\Alice\AppData\Roaming\MyCli\config.yaml but CLI displays it as /c/Users/Alice/... in some messages due to MSYS path conversions. Users copy paths and get 'file not found'.

Code uses std::filesystem::canonical and then outputs path.string(). When running under MSYS or Git Bash, canonical returns POSIX-flavored path. We should convert to native path format using std::filesystem::path::native() or use platform-specific formatting. func (s *Server) CreateThing(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    span, ctx := tracer.Start(ctx, "CreateThing")
    defer span.End()

    if err := s.store.Create(ctx, ...); err != nil {
        span.RecordError(err)
        http.Error(w, "internal", http.StatusInternalServerError)
        return

    s.metrics.Requests.WithLabelValues("CreateThing").Inc()

We need a detailed feature to preview Markdown content with server-side sanitization. The current client-side preview can be inconsistent. Add a POST /api/markdown/preview that renders GitHub-flavored markdown and sanitizes HTML via Bleach. Example expected code:

from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel
import markdown as md
import bleach

router = APIRouter()

class MarkdownPayload(BaseModel):
    text: str

ALLOWED_TAGS = bleach.sanitizer.ALLOWED_TAGS.union({'p','pre','span','img'})
ALLOWED_ATTRS = {**bleach.sanitizer.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES, 'img': ['src','alt']}

@router.post('/api/markdown/preview')
async def preview(payload: MarkdownPayload):
    html = md.markdown(payload.text, extensions=['extra', 'codehilite', 'toc'])
    safe = bleach.clean(html, tags=ALLOWED_TAGS, attributes=ALLOWED_ATTRS)
    return {'html': safe}

Also add rate limiting (5 req/s per IP) and tests for XSS cases.

Add i18n for the public pages. Use gettext catalogs and detect language from Accept-Language with a whitelist. Provide translations for en, es, fr, de. Include a language switcher in the footer and persist user preference in profile.

Add a simple AB testing framework: define experiments with variants and allocation ratios. Assign users deterministically by user_id hash. Expose an /api/experiments endpoint for the frontend to fetch active assignments. Log exposures and goal conversions.

Add support for chunked file uploads for files up to 2GB. Implement tus or a similar protocol: create, patch, head endpoints with resume support. Store chunk state in Redis and assemble in a background job on completion. Validate content hashes.

Add a data retention policy: automatically delete logs older than 90 days and anonymize user IPs after 30 days. Create a scheduled job and provide a dashboard with counts of records to be purged/anonymized. Make the retention window configurable via settings.
