Add a repro test and fix the lifetime/Arc usage.

Please add a cargo feature matrix test in CI ensuring combinations of features compile and tests run: default, minimal, grpc-only, wasm, no_std. Include a script that uses cargo hack to run the matrix locally and document it.

We need integration tests for ETag handling and conditional requests. Mock a server that returns 304 for If-None-Match and assert we correctly use the cache and surface a NotModified variant instead of treating it as an error.

A customer reported that our exponential backoff exceeds the maximum allowed deadline. Add a test verifying that the total delay for N retries never exceeds client.deadline. Use fake time and assert each sleep duration and cumulative budget.

Add tests for our streaming response body decoder using async_stream. Simulate chunked transfer with chunk boundaries splitting UTF-8 code points and ensure we handle them correctly without data loss or panics.

We’re missing tests for our SDK’s pagination iterator cancelation. If the consumer drops the stream early, we should ensure the HTTP connection is closed and no retries get scheduled. Add a test using drop and a weak counter to assert cleanup.

Add tests validating that our metrics exporter produces the correct counters and histograms for request outcomes. Use a test recorder and ensure labels are stable and low-cardinality. Include a regression for the doubled labels bug reported last week.

The SDK has an optional Redis cache feature. Add integration tests with a local Redis (testcontainers-rs) to verify TTL semantics, reconnection logic, and error mapping. Include a test for network hiccups with backoff and jitter.

I need tests for the CLI that wraps the SDK. Use assert_cmd to run the binary, feed JSON via stdin, and verify structured JSON output and non-zero exit codes on errors. Add snapshot tests and ensure they’re stable across platforms.

Our retry policy has a bug when Retry-After is a date. Add a unit test with a fixed Date header (RFC 7231 format) to verify parsing. Include both seconds and date forms and ensure we clamp to max_backoff.

Add a doc test and a real unit test for our new typed error hierarchy. Demonstrate matching on Error::Http(HttpError::Status(429)) and mapping to user-facing messages without losing the underlying context.

We should cover HTTP/2 settings behavior. Add tests that ensure the h2_keep_alive_interval is honored and that connections are re-established after GOAWAY. Mock the transport and assert we attempt reconnect within a bounded time.

We need a regression test for a panic that happens when building the Client without a base_url and then calling request(). The test should confirm we get a ConfigError at build time and not a late panic. Use trybuild to catch compile-time issues if possible.

Add tests to ensure our SDK cleanly handles very large JSON payloads (50MB+). Use a generated fixture and stream parsing with serde_json::Deserializer::from_reader. Ensure the memory footprint doesn’t blow up; assert peak allocations using allocation counters if feasible.

Introduce a hardened test for cancellation propagation: if the caller wraps a request in tokio::time::timeout and it elapses, make sure the underlying in-flight operations are canceled and sockets closed. Add assertions via a custom adapter that counts drops.

The wasm example test fails with Unhandled Promise Rejection when the request error isn’t converted to JsValue properly. Add a test that ensures Error implements Into<JsValue> with meaningful messages, and fix the conversion in wasm feature builds.

Add tests for our backoff jitter distribution to ensure uniformity bounds. Use statistical testing with a fixed RNG seed and assert the sample mean is within epsilon of expected. Provide a helper so the test remains deterministic.

We need a test that covers TLS client auth using rustls. Spin up a local server with a self-signed CA and client cert; verify handshake succeeds and that we present the correct certificate. Skip in CI for macOS if flaky, but run in Linux.
Please add tests verifying that our SDK respects the NO_COLOR convention and the --color flag in CLI output. Include cases for piped vs TTY stdout and ensure logs/tracing respect the color setting.

Add Miri to CI and ensure at least the core unit tests pass under miri. Fix or cfg-gate tests that use unsupported syscalls. Provide a guide for contributors to run cargo miri test locally with the right RUSTC_WRAPPER.
Add migration to rename users.full_name to display_name without data loss; update Zig models and API serializers accordingly.
Create migration to add message_reactions table with a composite unique index (message_id, user_id, emoji); ensure backward-compatible fallback for older app versions.
We need an offline-safe migration to add NOT NULL with default to posts.created_at; prevent app crash on devices with older cached posts.
Remove deprecated device_tokens table and backfill records into push_tokens; write reversible migration and clean up foreign keys referencing device_tokens.
Add a partial index on events(user_id, created_at DESC) and update query plans; include a migration guard for SQLite versions <3.35.

We need to introduce an accounts table to replace the legacy single-user assumption. The migration should backfill existing profile data from the settings blob into accounts and link existing sessions to the new account rows. Ensure this is a forward-only migration on first launch and add a downgrade path for internal beta testers who might revert.

Our beta users in APAC are seeing slow startup after the last update. The logs indicate schema validation checks are timing out. Please split the schema check from the migration runner so the migration itself is only evaluated if the schema hash changed. Also document the hash calculation method in the README so QA can verify.

The app is hitting a write-ahead log growth issue after we switched to WAL mode by default. We need a migration that sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL only for devices with free disk space > 200MB, and falls back to DELETE mode otherwise. Please add telemetry to record which mode is set so we can analyze from RemoteConfig.

We still have a ghost column comments.temp_text introduced in 1.8. It’s unused and bloating rows. Write a migration that copies data to comments.text, preserves FTS triggers, and drops the old column, with a safe rollback in case of failure.

We’re seeing inconsistencies in purchase_receipts due to a missing unique constraint on (transaction_id, platform). Add the constraint with conflict resolution that deduplicates rows by keeping the newest created_at, and write a script to clean existing duplicates.

The onboarding flow occasionally fails to create the initial local profile record because migrations run after we write the draft profile. Please make migration execution blocking before any writes. Add a boot-time preflight to check pending migrations and surface a toast if something is wrong.

We need to bump the schema version and add a migration to store push subscription scopes (alerts, badges, sounds). The migration should parse existing serialized JSON into columns and handle records with malformed payloads by setting defaults, logging a non-fatal error, and continuing.

We rely on implicit foreign keys in some tables and forgot to enable PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON after migrating. Add a post-migration step to enforce foreign keys and include a preflight check to detect orphan rows, logging counts by table so we can diagnose in Sentry.

We should add an index on notifications(read, created_at DESC) to improve the inbox load time. Create a migration that adds the index if it doesn’t exist, and verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN before/after. Include telemetry timing for the first three app launches post-migration.

The export feature fails when the migrations table has a partially applied record due to an app crash. Add a recovery migration that detects incomplete steps and retries them idempotently. Document the state machine and add unit tests for interrupted migrations.

Migration needed to support multi-tenant workspaces. Create workspace_members table, backfill current user as owner, and update all tables referencing user_id to also reference workspace_id where applicable. Keep existing queries working by introducing views.

We’re changing the primary key of cached_images from INTEGER to TEXT(content_hash). The migration should copy rows into a new table, rebuild indexes, and swap tables atomically. Also clean old blobs from disk that no longer match the new key scheme.

We have a collation mismatch causing inconsistent sorting of usernames on Android vs iOS builds. Add a migration to create a custom NOCASE collation and rebuild the index on profiles(username). Ensure Zig builds register the collation at db open.

Add a migration that introduces a pending_sync table for offline create/update operations. Backfill from the old sync_queue JSON blob, preserving order and retry counts. Include a validator that flags unknown operation types to Sentry at info level.

We need to enforce CHECK constraints on the locations table to prevent invalid lat/lng values. Write a migration adding CHECK(abs(lat) <= 90 AND abs(lng) <= 180), and resolve existing violations by clamping and logging the affected row ids.

On startup after 2.3.0, a subset of users get a crash in the migration that adds the conversations.last_read_at column. The crash seems tied to a transaction not being committed when an index already exists. Could someone review the transaction boundaries? We probably need to wrap the schema changes in a single deferred transaction and guard CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS. Also, confirm we’re not running PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON in the middle of the DDL, which might be causing the lock escalation.

We shipped an FTS5 virtual table for messages but forgot to adjust the tokenizer to ascii + porter. We should write a migration that drops and recreates the FTS table with the correct tokenizer, then reindexes from the base table. Make sure the migration yields periodically so we don’t ANR on low-end devices; maybe batch in 2k increments and flush.

We’ve got mismatched enum values for subscription_status after the analytics schema refactor. Add a migration that normalizes existing values (trialing/active/grace/expired) and introduces a CHECK constraint. Also update the API adapter so serialized values match the new canonical form.

Some users see duplicated rows in the recently_viewed table due to a bad unique index. Please add a migration to rebuild the unique index on (user_id, item_type, item_id) with ON CONFLICT REPLACE semantics and remove bad duplicates. Provide a one-time compaction after.

We’re going to encrypt the SQLite database using SQLCipher on devices with Biometric unlock enabled. Add a migration that runs a key change, reindexes, and validates PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check. Provide a no-op fallback on devices that don’t support the feature.

We want to consolidate attachment metadata into a single attachments table referenced from posts and messages. Add the table, migrate existing foreign keys, and create a trigger to keep counts in sync. Make sure background media downloads don’t break mid-migration.

We need to split address into street, city, region, and postal_code. The migration must parse freeform addresses where possible and keep the original in address_raw for fallback. Add a server sync patch to avoid resending unchanged addresses.

Please add a migration guard that checks sqlite_version >= 3.35 before using generated columns for analytics_rollup. If unsupported, create regular columns and triggers to simulate the behavior. Log which path was taken to analytics.log for analysis.

We’re missing ON DELETE CASCADE on child tables related to workspace deletion. Write a migration that rebuilds affected tables with the correct foreign keys. Ensure the migration captures and replays pending sync operations referencing those rows before deletion.

We have a rare deadlock when running the migration that moves favorites to bookmarks. It might stem from a background thread reading bookmarks while the transaction runs. Update the migration runner to acquire an app-wide migration mutex and suspend read transactions.

The last release included a migration to add json_extract indices, but on some devices json1 isn’t compiled in and the migration fails. Update the migration to test json1 via SELECT json('[]') and skip those indices if unavailable. Provide a soft warning only.

The migration runner sometimes mixes stdout/stderr logs and we can't diagnose failures. Add structured logging with timestamps and migration_id, and record the duration of each step. On error, dump last 100 lines of db logs to a migration_failures table for later upload.

Users who installed v1.0 and upgraded straight to v2.7 have a gap in migration ordering that causes an index to refer to a dropped column. Add a squashed migration that detects this legacy path and applies the correct sequence, using temp tables to reconcile state.

We notice that our migrations assume UTC for created_at defaults, but some records were created before the timezone decision. Add a data migration that normalizes timestamps to UTC, stores original_offset, and updates queries to derive local display time consistently.

After enabling strict mode, the comment_count trigger on posts fails in legacy databases. Write a migration that recreates triggers with proper INSERT/DELETE handling and validates counts after. Include a repair script that recalculates comment_count for all posts.

We’re going to change the primary key on downloads to a ULID string. Please write an online migration that copies rows in batches, preserves foreign keys, and switches references via a mapping table. Add app-level adapters to support both keys during rollout.

Can we add a migration to compress large JSON payloads in api_cache using zstd and store a content_encoding column? Be careful to avoid double compressing and add a CHECK to ensure only text/json payloads are compressed.

A migration introducing the reading_progress table is failing on devices with low disk space. We need a staged approach that checks disk usage, frees obsolete thumbnails, and then proceeds. On failure, we should roll back cleanly and surface a user-facing retry prompt.

Introduce a migration to create a feature_flags table driven by remote config, with default values for cold start. Backfill flags from known defaults in code. Also add a migration test that asserts unknown flags do not crash the parser.

We have a pending migration to add a unique constraint on device_settings per device_id. Please ensure the migration tolerates devices that somehow wrote null device_id. Those should be fixed by populating a derived id from platform and vendor info.

We must migrate the legacy sync token from settings.kv into a proper sync_state table with last_sync_at and cursor fields. Ensure the migration is idempotent and does not reset incremental sync progress if partially applied on earlier crashes.

We want to replace our homegrown migrations with a versioned zig-based migrator that loads SQL from embedded assets. Add the migration runner, port existing migrations, and provide an adapter to run additional pre/post hooks per platform for file permissions.

We need to implement a safe, resumable migration that rebuilds the messages_fts table and replays incoming new messages from a buffer to avoid missing updates. Provide code to buffer inserts while FTS is rebuilding, then drain the buffer within the same transaction.

Add migration for referral codes: create referrals table, add referral_code to users, enforce uniqueness, and backfill codes for existing users without clobbering already-set values. Generate codes deterministically from uid + salt to ensure consistency across devices.

We discovered that our purchase_renewal table has incorrect FK references pointing to an outdated purchases table. The migration must fix the foreign key to the new subscriptions table and repair existing rows using a join with transaction_id to map to subscription_id.

Here’s a reproducible crash in the migration that adds NOT NULL to posts.author_id on devices with drafts:

App startup stuck at the splash screen if the migration lock isn’t released due to a crash. We need a watchdog that detects a stale lock and offers to retry. Add a sentinel file approach, and ensure the migration runner writes progress markers. Provide a CLI to inspect state via zig test or a small debug menu.

The API now returns nullable phone on profiles, but our migration set phone to NOT NULL. We need to adjust: make phone nullable, backfill only verified numbers into a new phone_verified table, and update GraphQL resolvers to read from the new table. Include a down migration path for QA.

We’re testing a migration that adds a generated column last_active_date(date(last_active_at)). On older devices, generated columns aren’t supported. Please implement feature detection and create a real column + trigger fallback. Show both code paths in the migrator with proper logging.

We introduced a migration to move images to a content-addressed store. Some users report massive storage bloat post-upgrade. Add a verification step that removes unreferenced blobs after migrating rows. Provide Zig code to scan references in posts, messages, and cached_images and delete orphans in batches with a progress callback.

On fresh installs, the migrator tries to ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN liked, then fails because posts doesn’t exist yet. We need to ensure initial schema creation path includes all columns, with migrations only for upgrades. Add a bootstrap path that loads schema.sql for new dbs and writes the base version into migrations table.

When migration fails halfway through adding indices, our retry path drops and recreates indices blindly, causing extra startup time. Improve idempotency by probing sqlite_master to check index definitions and only create missing ones. Add an explain/tracing log of what changed.

Implement migration to move pinned_chats ordering from float ranks to integer ranks with gaps (step=1000). Convert existing ranks by sorting and assigning new sequence numbers. Provide Zig code that computes sequence numbers in-memory and updates rows in a single transaction.

Our enum mapping in Zig uses a packed enum that changed representation. The migration reading raw bytes from user_status table is now wrong. Provide a data migration that maps old integer codes to the new enum via CASE statements, and update Zig decoding to use explicit casts.

Migration 20241020_add_sessions unique index conflicts with anonymous sessions created offline. Write a migration that detects anonymous session rows and merges them with authenticated rows after login. Supply conflict resolution logic and a replay of pending analytics events.

Add a migration test harness in Zig that runs migrations against an in-memory SQLite DB and verifies schema invariants (FKs on, pragma settings, index coverage). Include a couple of property-based tests ensuring idempotency when migrations are re-run.

We need a migration that adds a device_capabilities table and backfills supported features (biometric, nfc, camera) from the runtime probe. Provide platform-specific hooks in Zig to read capabilities at migration time and write rows only once, guarded by a versioned flag.
Refactor the IPC handlers to a dedicated module with strict typings. Current implementation spreads handlers across multiple files and uses any in a few places.
Please extract our file system utilities into a pure TypeScript library with proper interfaces and remove all Node-specific calls from the renderer.
Unify our error handling strategy by replacing thrown strings with typed Error classes throughout the app.
Replace legacy callback-based clipboard utilities with async/await wrappers and centralize them in a platform adapter.
Consolidate duplicated logger setup across main and preload into a single factory with typed log levels.

Our Electron auto-update flow mixes UI concerns with networking code. Can we refactor the update check into a service that exposes a typed event emitter and keep UI updates in the renderer only? Document the public interface and add unit tests for event sequences.

We need to clean up the settings state logic. It's split between Redux and local component state. Propose a small refactor to consolidate into a single source of truth (likely Redux Toolkit), remove dead selectors, and add memoization where needed.

The shortcut registration module registers accelerators in multiple places. Let's refactor to a single ShortcutRegistry with a declarative config file and lazy registration when windows gain focus. Consider cross-platform differences.

Our API client has inconsistent naming and response types. Standardize method names (getProject, createProject, etc.), introduce a typed Result<T, E> return, and deprecate the old promise shape with a migration path.
We’re leaking file descriptors on Windows when opening large projects. Please refactor the project loader pipeline into a stream-based approach and ensure all handles are disposed deterministically.

Refactor the theme system: right now we inline CSS variables in multiple React components. We should centralize theme tokens in a typed Theme object, use context, and eliminate any direct document.documentElement mutations from components. Ensure dark mode toggle only triggers a single repaint.

The preload script exports too many globals. Please encapsulate window.api methods behind a typed IPC bridge with validation, and switch to contextIsolation-friendly patterns. Include examples of narrowing responses with discriminated unions.

We’ve got multiple ad-hoc retry loops for network calls. Introduce a small composable retryWithBackoff utility with typed options and replace all hand-rolled retries. Make sure cancellation via AbortController works across the app.

We’re getting inconsistent durations in performance marks due to duplicate mark names. Refactor the performance instrumentation to a light wrapper that ensures unique mark names and provides a strongly typed enum for phases.

The SQLite data access layer mixes SQL strings inline with business logic. Extract SQL queries to a repository layer with prepared statements, and add a small query builder helper. Keep transactions explicit and typed.

Please refactor the renderer store modules to use Redux Toolkit with createSlice and createAsyncThunk. Our current hand-written reducers are verbose and error-prone. Keep type safety for thunk payloads and draft mutation patterns.

We have multiple places formatting dates with different libraries (date-fns, Luxon, and manual). Consolidate to date-fns, create a small time.ts utility, and remove dead code. Add locale-awareness and UTC normalization.

The file watcher debouncing is duplicated in three places. Centralize it into a WatchService that exposes an Observable-like interface with typed event payloads. Replace bespoke debounce logic with a single implementation.
Refactor the window management to a declarative map of windows instead of imperative construction scattered around. Include lazy load for heavy windows and unify per-window preload scripts.
We still use deprecated remote module patterns in a few places. Remove all remote usage, refactor to IPC calls with typed channels, and add a small documentation section on safe IPC patterns.

We expose too many globals via process.env sprinkled across the codebase. Move to a Config service that reads env once, validates it, and exposes typed getters. Replace all process.env access with Config. Also inject Config into services rather than importing it directly to aid testing.

The current test suite mocks fs and path inconsistently. Introduce a FileSystem interface with methods we actually use, provide a NodeFileSystem implementation, and refactor modules to depend on the interface. In tests, provide an InMemoryFileSystem. This should reduce brittle Jest module mocks.

We’ve seen crashes due to unhandled promise rejections in the main process. Introduce a top-level unhandledRejection handler that routes to our logger and shows a diagnostics dialog in dev. Refactor async IPC handlers to always return Result types rather than throwing.

Example stack:

UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'C:\\tmp\\cfg.json'
    at Object.openSync (fs.js:462:3)
    at ...

Stop throwing; propagate via typed errors.

The localization layer loads JSON files on demand from the renderer using fs, which breaks sandboxing. Refactor to preload-driven resource loading with a typed i18n service in main that caches translations. The renderer should request strings via IPC or receive preloaded bundles. Remove all direct fs access in the renderer.

Our drag-and-drop implementation writes temp files synchronously to disk. Refactor to use async operations, move logic into a dedicated DragDropService, and ensure we clean up temp files on app quit. Add a typed TempFileHandle to track lifecycle.

The dependency injection container is hand-rolled and magic. Replace with a small explicit registry and constructor injection. Define interfaces for services, remove service locator usage, and refactor consumers to accept dependencies via parameters. This will make unit tests simpler.

We have two different JSON serialization strategies for app state. Standardize on a single stable stringify/parse with revivers for Dates. Provide a serializer module and refactor import/export to use it. Add tests to ensure backward compatibility with v1 exports.

Renderer startup bundles are large. Refactor shared utilities used only in the settings window into a lazy-loaded chunk. Use dynamic import() with explicit webpack/electron-builder hints. Ensure types flow correctly and avoid any usage of require in renderer code.

The app’s context menu is built imperatively for each window. Create a menu definition schema with role-based items and a builder function that converts to Electron Menu. Move platform-specific differences behind feature flags. Add unit tests for menu structure with snapshots.

Our window resize persistence logic writes to disk on every resize event. Introduce throttling and a WindowState service that batches writes. Refactor components to call saveWindowState(id, bounds) and read on creation. Ensure types include display scale factor for multi-monitor setups.

Please extract feature flag checks into a single typed module with compile-time constants for stable flags and runtime checks for experimental ones. Replace scattered if (process.env.FEATURE_X) with Flag.isEnabled('feature-x') and ensure type-safe keys.

Refactor the command palette to use a typed registry of commands with metadata (id, title, shortcut, handler). Replace ad-hoc arrays and strings. Provide type-safe registration and ensure command handlers can be async with error boundaries.

The project’s ESLint config is outdated and allows implicit any in several places. Update the config and refactor the code to satisfy noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, and no-floating-promises. Add tsconfig.base.json and per-target tsconfigs for main, preload, and renderer.

The document autosave timer uses setInterval sprinkled across modules. Create an AutosaveScheduler with start/stop and a typed callback list. Use NodeJS.Timer types, add pause during heavy operations, and refactor modules to use the scheduler rather than their own timers.

Bug observed:

Possible memory leak: 32 intervals active after switching projects repeatedly.

Current global state for selections uses a mutable object exported from a module:

export const selection = { ids: [] as string[] };

Components mutate it directly, causing race conditions. Refactor to a Redux slice or event emitter model with immutable updates. Provide a selection API:

select(ids: string[])
clear()
subscribe(listener)
get()

Ensure types enforce string IDs only.

We should refactor the FileOpen dialog flow. Logic currently lives in a React component and calls Electron APIs directly, which breaks tests with contextIsolation. Move dialog invocations to main and expose an IPC call returning a typed file handle. Update the component to call window.api.openFile().

Refactor the DB access to use better typing with Drizzle ORM (or knex with TypeScript). Replace raw SQL building in strings. Add a migration to enforce NOT NULL where the code expects it. Ensure the repository layer exposes typed methods and narrows columns correctly.

Current buggy query:

await db.run(`INSERT INTO projects VALUES ('${id}', '${name}', '${path}')`); // SQL injection risk

We need to split the massive types.d.ts into domain-specific modules with exports. Right now the global namespace pollution causes name clashes. Create a types package with explicit exports, enable typeRoots properly, and refactor imports across the app.

Refactor the packaging scripts for electron-builder to separate config per platform and ensure type safety in the build scripts. Move scripts from JS to TS with ts-node/register, define a BuildConfig type, and avoid reading JSON synchronously at runtime.

Our error boundaries in the renderer are class-based and duplicated. Replace with a single ErrorBoundary component using React 18 patterns and a typed FallbackRender prop. Ensure it catches errors from Suspense as well. Remove duplicate boundaries in child trees.

The retry logic for DB connections is copy-pasted. Introduce a retry module with exponential backoff and jitter. Ensure TypeScript types propagate the return type of the retried function. Replace all occurrences and add tests for cancellation.

Example API:

retry(async () => connect(), { retries: 5, onRetry(err, attempt) { ... } })

We should refactor the feature toggles UI to derive from a schema rather than hard-coded checkboxes. Define a Feature definition array with id, label, description, default. Render dynamically and bind to a typed settings slice. Remove duplicated checkbox components and effects.

The import/export wizards use a shared mutable global for progress. Replace with an observable store (like Zustand with TS or RxJS) and derive progress in a selector. Add types for progress phases and refactor consumers to subscribe instead of reading globals. This removes race conditions when multiple imports run.

Refactor the scheduler that runs background tasks. It currently uses setTimeout recursively and can drift. Introduce a TaskScheduler with a priority queue, typed tasks, and cancellation tokens. Ensure tasks can be persisted across restarts by serializing descriptors to disk with a schema guard.

The current path normalization uses path.normalize inconsistently between Windows and POSIX. Create a PathService with typed methods (toSystemPath, toPosix, ensureTrailingSlash) and refactor modules to use it. Add tests with sample paths to avoid regressions. Remove embedded regex hacks.

The monolithic SyncService file is 1200 lines and mixes websocket, REST, and conflict resolution. Split into modules with explicit interfaces:

- Transport (WebSocketClient, RestClient)
- SyncCoordinator
- ConflictResolver
- StateStore

Define types for domain events and results. Add unit tests for conflict resolution scenarios. Keep the public API stable: start(), stop(), forceSync().

Refactor notification handling. We create Notification objects in the renderer and the main process differently. Create a NotificationService interface and implement platform adapters (macOS, Windows, Linux). Ensure the renderer requests notifications via IPC with typed payloads and permissions checks. Remove direct new Notification() in components.

The main process crash reporter wraps Sentry with any types. Add proper TypeScript types, split initialization from capture logic, and refactor to a captureException(error: AppError, context?: object) signature. Migrate callers. Ensure breadcrumbs are attached from the logger via a transport integration.

Stack trace when opening Preferences crashes due to circular JSON in logger meta:

Error: Converting circular structure to JSON
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
    at FileTransport.log (.../logger.ts:88:12)
    at Logger.error (.../logger.ts:54:5)

Refactor logger transports to detect and safely serialize circular structures using a replacer. Create a safeStringify utility and replace JSON.stringify calls. Add types to ensure meta is unknown and narrowed before serialization.

Renderer build shows type drift errors after TS 5.6 upgrade:

src/hooks/use-config.ts:41:13 - error TS2775: Assertions require every name in the call target to be declared with an explicit type annotation.

Refactor assertion utilities to explicit function types instead of const assertions, e.g. change:

export const assert = (cond: any, msg?: string) => { if (!cond) throw new Error(msg); }

to:

export function assert(cond: unknown, msg?: string): asserts cond {}

Sweep for similar issues and update types accordingly.
Enable mTLS between the gateway and the C API service and enforce client cert validation with CRL/OCSP checking.
Add rate limiting to the /v1/upload endpoint to mitigate brute force attempts. Token bucket per API key, with 429 on overage.
Replace SHA-1 in our request signing with HMAC-SHA256 and rotate keys. Keep a dual-verify window for 2 weeks.
Harden CORS on the admin endpoints to only allow our dashboard origin and disallow credentials for public APIs.
Turn on -fstack-protector-strong and -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 in our default CMake release profile.

The C API service currently loads its TLS private key from disk; we need to move to in-memory loading from our KMS and ensure zeroization. The key should never be written to tempfile or exposed in logs. Add a secure_memzero function for cleanup and ensure all error paths wipe the buffer before returning.

We need to add structured audit logs for all authz failures. Include API key id, hashed client IP, endpoint, and reason. Make sure sensitive headers (e.g., Authorization) are redacted before logging, and that logs are JSON with a stable schema to feed into SIEM.

The /v1/transform endpoint accepts a JSON schema parameter that we deserialize and use to allocate buffers. We’ve had an out-of-bounds read in prod under load. Please bound-check user-provided sizes, cap allocations to 8MB per request, and return 413 for oversized payloads. Add integration tests and fuzz inputs.

Our HTTP server currently reflects raw error messages from parsing failures back to the client. Strip internal file paths and compile flags from error bodies, return generic 400, and move detailed info to server logs with trace IDs.
CMake should enforce PIE and RELRO for the service binaries. Update toolchain files to set -fPIE -pie -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,relro and fail the build if the linker flags are missing.

We’re leaking file descriptors under TLS renegotiation failures, causing resource exhaustion. Repro: run 10k aborted handshakes. lsof shows thousands of sockets in CLOSE_WAIT. Please ensure close() is called on all error paths after SSL_shutdown, and set SO_LINGER to avoid lingering. Add tests using tc netem to inject handshake aborts.

The request parser uses sscanf for integers, which allows negative values for size headers and wraps around. Replace with strtoumax and explicit bounds. Show before/after diff, and add unit tests for edge cases like 0, UINT_MAX, and overflow strings.

Add CSP and strict transport security headers to responses served by our built-in mini status page. Also disable directory listing. Ensure headers are only added on HTTPS connections, and add tests for correct max-age and includeSubDomains.

Our gRPC C gateway does not validate :authority or :path pseudo-headers, allowing header smuggling between proxies. Add strict validation and reject requests with multiple content-length headers, invalid pseudo-header order, or uppercase header names. Include compliance with RFC 7540.

The PEM loader accepts PKCS#1 RSA keys; we need to reject keys smaller than 2048 bits and migrate to P-256 ECDSA by default. Add runtime checks using OpenSSL EVP_PKEY_bits and log warnings for RSA < 3072. Document the migration path.

We discovered that our error logger prints raw JSON payloads when request parsing fails. This risks PII exposure. Implement field-level redaction for common sensitive keys (password, ssn, token), and truncate logged payloads at 2KB. Add a redact_payload function with a configurable allowlist.

Our DB connector builds SQL from query params. We need to switch to prepared statements and parameter binding in the C libpq layer. For example:

```c
snprintf(sql, sizeof(sql), "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email='%s'", email);
```

Replace with PQprepare/PQexecPrepared, and add escaping tests. Reject any query with embedded NULs.

The service’s WebSocket upgrade path does not assert Origin for browser-based clients, opening CSRF over WS. Implement an origin check against config allowlist, and require token re-auth on upgrade. Add integration tests with curl and browser headers.

Harden our base Docker image: run as non-root, drop NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, enable seccomp default profile, and mount the /keys directory as read-only. Validate with container-scanning CI and refuse to start when keydir permissions are too broad (chmod 0700).

Enable ASLR hardening checks in CI by verifying binary properties with readelf and eu-readelf. Also ensure -fno-common and -Wl,--no-undefined are set. Create a CI step failing if PIE/RELRO not present.

Our HSM integration retries on transient failures but logs the decrypted plaintext on the second attempt (debug log). Remove any logging of secrets, replace with ciphertext IDs, and gate all sensitive logs behind a build-time SECURE_LOGS flag that defaults to off. Add tests verifying logs do not contain sensitive substrings.

Implement per-route access control lists. The current router only authenticates but doesn’t authorize. Create a role bitmask and map endpoints to required roles. On mismatch return 403 with a generic message. Ensure the authorization decision is logged with trace ID and not the user’s raw token.

We found that our C client library stores API tokens in ~/.capi/config with 0644 permissions. Change default to 0600 and add a self-test that refuses to load tokens if permissions are too open. On Windows, use CryptProtectData for storage.

TLS session tickets are using a static key for too long. Rotate the ticket encryption key every 24 hours, keep a two-key window for decryption, and store keys only in memory. On restart, do not persist; re-handshake. Add config for rotation interval.

The protobuf deserializer trusts length fields and doesn’t enforce total message limit. Enforce a max message size (e.g., 4MB) at the framing layer and reject nested messages that exceed depth 64. Add a failure metric and test corpora for pathological nesting.

We need to adopt secure_zero_memory semantics across the codebase. Our current memset is optimized out by the compiler in some builds. Introduce a portable secure_memzero function using volatile pointer and call it on key buffers, HMAC states, and decrypted material. Verify via test that memory is zeroed using a post-read.

Our error page handler reflects user-provided query parameters into HTML without encoding. Even though this is a service, the built-in diagnostics UI can be opened in browser. Sanitize with HTML escaping and use a Content Security Policy to block inline scripts.

The request ID generation uses rand() seeded with time(NULL). Replace with cryptographically secure IDs using OS RNG (getrandom on Linux, CryptGenRandom on Windows) and encode as base64url. Add entropy checks in tests and ensure RNG failures abort request safely.

Upgrade OpenSSL to 3.0.x and replace deprecated SHA1 EVP usage. While at it, enable FIPS mode when available. Add runtime checks that fail startup if FIPS required=true and module not available. Provide a migration doc.

Please add a global timeout and watchdog for JSON parsing, as we’ve observed CPU pegged on crafted inputs. Here is a reproducer and callstack:

```
$ ./capi_svc --port 8080
[info] listening on 0.0.0.0:8080
[warn] high CPU usage detected
^C
# perf top shows json_parse_value hot loop
```

```c
static int parse_string(const char *p) {
    while (*p && *p != '"') { /* no progress on invalid utf-8 */ }
    return 0;
}
```

Add iteration limits and bail out with 400 on malformed UTF-8. Consider switching to a hardened JSON library with O(1) progress guarantees.
Add IP allowlisting to the admin RPC port and bind it to 127.0.0.1 by default. Today it binds 0.0.0.0:9090. Update config parsing to default to loopback and error if exposed without TLS.

CSRF protection for the built-in UI: add a double-submit token tied to the user’s session cookie, with SameSite=Lax and secure flags. Validate token on mutating requests and rotate on login. Ensure error messages do not leak token values.

Data at rest encryption: our SQLite cache file is plaintext. Integrate SQLCipher or at least file-system level encryption with key from KMS. Use PRAGMA cipher_page_size, cipher_kdf_iter to harden defaults. Ensure WAL files are encrypted as well.

We should harden our URL parser against scheme confusion. For example, javascript://example.com/ should never be allowed. Validate schemes against a strict allowlist (http, https, ws, wss) and reject embedded credentials in URLs.

Add a post-quantum ready KEM option (e.g., Kyber via liboqs) behind a feature flag for internal testing. Ensure we negotiate only with mutual support and record telemetry. Validate that enabling does not regress performance or introduce weaker ciphersuites.

We need to sandbox image parsing in the thumbnail endpoint to protect against malformed inputs. Run the decoder in a seccomp-bpf filtered subprocess with a 100ms CPU and 8MB memory cap. Communicate via a pipe and validate input size before fork.

Our configuration loader accepts environment variable expansions and executes backticks in some paths by calling system("echo ..."). Remove any shell evaluation and implement a safe expansion that only replaces ${VAR} with getenv values. Add tests to prove backticks are not executed.

Implement structured input validation for all integer request fields using a single module. Right now we have scattered atoi uses susceptible to overflow/underflow. Create parse_uint32 and parse_size functions with strict range checks and uniform error codes.

We have duplicate handling of Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked which enables request smuggling behind Nginx. Normalize by rejecting requests that specify both, and ensure we consume the entire body on error to avoid desync. Include regression tests with httptoolkit.

Our logging gRPC interceptor attaches the full metadata map including Authorization and Cookie. Redact sensitive keys before logging and allow an allowlist of safe headers. Add a benchmark to ensure low overhead.
Implement HTTP Strict-Transport-Security preload, and add Expect-CT deprecation handling. Also, add Alt-Svc only on TLS connections to avoid downgrade attacks. Verify via securityheaders.com in CI.

Add automatic key rotation for API keys stored in Postgres. Introduce a created_at and last_used_at, and have the service refuse keys older than 180 days unless explicitly exempted. Provide a dual-key window and migration script. Ensure queries use parameterized statements.

We need to add a permission system for our webhook secrets so that only the webhook module can read them. Right now, any component can call secrets_get("webhook"). Introduce namespaces and per-component ACLs in the secrets manager, and audit calls.

There’s a stack trace on malformed multipart form data leading to read beyond boundary. Logs:

```
[error] multipart.c:242 boundary not found
[segv] SIGSEGV at 0x00000004 pc=0x55a1bd1a
```

Code snippet:

```c
char *p = strstr(buf, boundary);
size_t len = p - buf; // p may be NULL
memcpy(out, buf, len);
```

Add null checks and fail with 400. Add fuzz tests and size checks to cap total parts and per-part size.

Please add a zero-trust policy for inter-service calls: include a signed, short-lived service token in x-service-assertion with audience and expiry. Validate clock skew and audience. Cache validation results for 30s with LRU and fail closed when cache errors occur.

The base64 decoder accepts non-canonical padding and ignores invalid characters, which can lead to confused deputy in our signature verification. Switch to a strict decoder that rejects non-canonical inputs. Add tests for malformed padding and overlong encodings.

Refactor our thread pool to avoid timing side channels on authentication failures. Ensure that 401 responses return in constant time within a small jitter window, regardless of whether the API key exists. Add histogram tests and ensure not to log per-key timing.

We need to implement OCSP stapling for our TLS endpoints and prefer Must-Staple certs. Cache OCSP responses, refresh proactively, and refuse to start if no fresh staple is available when require_staple=true. Log stapling status with metrics.

Enable fuzzing targets for parsers (HTTP headers, JSON, multipart) and integrate with OSS-Fuzz. Add sanitizer builds (-fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined) and seed corpora from production samples after PII scrubbing. Ensure CI runs a 60s fuzz smoke test per target.

The CLI tool prints detailed certificate info including subject and SAN to stdout. We should scrub PII when running in diagnostic mode unless --verbose is set. Also, add a --redact flag to enforce anonymization.

Our caching layer sets Cache-Control: public for responses that include user-scoped data. Use Cache-Control: private, no-store on any response derived from an API key or token. Add a middleware that sets safe defaults and override only when safe.

Implement audit-proof deletion for sensitive logs: add a configurable retention and secure deletion using POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED followed by overwrite on spinning disks where possible, or rely on encrypted partition key rotation. Provide documentation and a test plan.

We should block requests with Unicode confusables in header names to prevent header spoofing in mixed stacks. Normalize headers to lowercase ASCII and reject if any non-ASCII present. Add tests for homoglyphs like ‘а’ (Cyrillic).

Please add a secure password hashing module for admin passwords using Argon2id with tuned memory and time costs. Migrate existing bcrypt hashes gradually, verifying on login and upgrading hash format. Store parameters alongside hash and add a versioned hash scheme.
Add a zero-allocation path for parsing small JSON payloads. Right now our parse method allocates multiple intermediate strings; can we reuse buffers and reduce GC pressure?
Replace Mutex with a lock-free structure in the cache fetch path to avoid contention under high concurrency. Consider Concurrent::Map or atomic reference updates.
Make pagination helpers lazy (Enumerator::Lazy) to avoid materializing arrays when not strictly necessary.
Provide a fast path for frozen string inputs in normalizers to skip dup and encoding checks.
Use IO.copy_stream in our file downloader to avoid Ruby-level read/write loops.

We noticed CPU spikes when using the instrumentation hooks. Could we make event emission conditional and entirely no-op when no subscribers are present? Ideally, the code path should be zero cost when instrumentation is disabled. Some quick profiling shows that just building the event payload hashes accounts for ~8% of runtime in hot paths.

The Redis-based memoization backend is causing extra RTTs due to separate exists/get calls. Can we refactor to use GETEX or a Lua script to atomically fetch and extend TTL? This should save a round trip per fetch on cache hits and reduce contention during bursts.

Our HTML sanitizer adds 3–5 ms per call for small inputs. Is there a way to precompile the regex patterns and reuse them across calls? If the library already does this, maybe we can expose an API to inject a compiled sanitizer instance that we can reuse across requests.

When running on JRuby, the current File.mtime checks cause a lot of I/O. Could we introduce a configuration flag to disable timestamp checks and rely on a digest manifest? This is for environments where files are immutable at runtime.

Can we add a streaming API for CSV writing that avoids building the entire string in memory? Something like yielding to a provided IO and using StringIO as a fallback. We hit memory spikes on large datasets.

The ActiveSupport::Notifications integration is adding overhead in our benchmarks. When no subscribers are registered, we're still allocating payload hashes and strings that get thrown away. Propose introducing a feature flag or internal fast path so that when notifications are globally disabled or there are zero subscribers for the event, we skip building payloads. We measured a ~10% throughput improvement in a JSON API endpoint when we stubbed out notifications entirely. Ideally, the public API remains unchanged, but the hot path is allocation-free in the no-subscriber case.

Our pagination library does N+1 queries for counts when used with grouped relations. While this is functionally correct, it becomes a bottleneck on large tables. Could we add an option to estimate counts using PostgreSQL reltuples stats or maintain a rolling approximate count cache? We’re fine trading off exactness for performance in some environments, but we’d like a pluggable strategy rather than forking.

The retry middleware currently sleeps with Kernel.sleep even for very short delays, which doesn’t play nicely with Async/Fiber-based runtimes. Is it possible to integrate with an event loop timer (async-io) or at least make the sleeper injectable so we can use a non-blocking wait? This should reduce tail latency under load in our HTTP client.

Could we add a batch fetch interface to our key-value adapter so callers can request multiple keys at once? Many stores (Redis MGET, Memcached multi-get) support this. Our current loop over get allocates per-call and performs multiple round trips.

Please add an option to freeze returned strings from the tokenizer to avoid repeated string allocations on consumers who immediately freeze anyway. Ideally opt-in and documented, and we should benchmark the impact on GC.

Our internal benchmarks show that the template renderer is allocating lots of strings due to string interpolation in loops. Suggest adding an option to precompile templates into Procs and reuse them across requests. Also consider enabling frozen string literals by default in generated templates. This should significantly reduce allocated objects and improve CPU efficiency.

We’re using your HTTP client and noticed it builds the full response body in memory before yielding to the caller. For large downloads, this is causing memory spikes and longer GC pauses. Could you provide a fully streaming response API that lets us process chunks as they arrive? Bonus points if it cooperates with Rack hijack or IO-like interfaces so we can pipe into IO.copy_stream without userland loops.

We have a performance regression when upgrading to Ruby 3.3 related to keyword arguments in tight loops. The library uses keyword args extensively for internal helpers. Can we introduce a positional fast path for internal calls or refactor hot methods to accept a single options hash to avoid keyword arg overhead? We’re seeing ~7–9% request latency increase compared to 3.2.

When running on YJIT, methods with lots of megamorphic call sites seem to deopt frequently in your routing layer. Maybe we can cache dispatch decisions per path pattern to reduce method lookups? A small LRU keyed by regex+verb might help stabilize performance without changing API semantics.

The JSON encoder falls back to JSON::Pure on platforms without the C extension. Could we detect and warn, but also attempt to load Oj or MultiJson if available? We need a drop-in way to get native performance when c-exts aren’t present.

The following hot path in our library's normalizer is doing a lot of allocations and seems to be CPU bound. Can we refactor to reduce object creation and possibly use frozen constants?

Benchmark results (Ruby 3.2.2, x86_64-linux):

  Normalizer.normalize (baseline):
    4.12k (±2.5%) i/s - 20.7k in 5.024s

  After inlining freeze and avoiding gsub with regex backref:
    6.89k (±2.1%) i/s - 34.7k in 5.034s

Code snippet currently:

```ruby
module Normalizer
  module_function

  def normalize(input)
    str = input.to_s.dup
    str = str.encode('UTF-8', invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    str = str.gsub(/\s+/, ' ')
    str.strip!
    str.downcase!
    str
  end
end
```

Proposed change: reuse a single SPACE regex constant, skip dup if input is already String and not tainted, and use tr_s(' ', ' ') after a fast whitespace collapse using a buffer. Also consider returning frozen strings when configured.

Our Redis cache adapter performs JSON.parse with symbolize_names: true, which allocates a lot of symbols and increases memory. Suggest defaulting to strings, and only symbolizing when explicitly requested. Provide a migration note in the changelog. Here’s a flamegraph showing JSON.generate/parse taking ~30% of request time due to allocations. We’d like to reduce GC time by avoiding symbol creation in hot paths.

We suspect the library’s HTTP retry backoff uses Random.rand per attempt, causing significant overhead under high throughput. Can we replace with a fast xorshift or splittable PRNG seeded per-thread and expose an interface for deterministic seeds in test? Also make the backoff calculation allocation-free by avoiding building fractional floats unnecessarily.

The library’s custom logger builds log messages with string interpolation even when log level is above the threshold. Example:

```ruby
logger.debug { "Fetched #{rows.size} rows for key=#{key}" }
```

But internally, it calls .to_s on the block result regardless of log level. Can we lazily evaluate only when level enabled? This will drop unnecessary allocations on prod where debug is off. Please add a benchmark to ensure debug-off path is near-zero overhead.

We’re seeing severe slowdown on JRuby due to synchronized blocks around a Concurrent::Map we use for memoization. The code:

```ruby
@memo_mutex.synchronize do
  @cache[key] ||= compute_value(key)
end
```

Under high concurrency, this causes contention. Suggest using Concurrent::Map#compute_if_absent or AtomicReference + CAS loop to avoid coarse-grained locks. Also ensure compute_value is not called more than once per key under contention. Provide tests for race conditions.

Please consider compiling frequently-used regexes at load time and freezing them. Example:

```ruby
PATTERN = /
  ^(?<scheme>https?):\/\/
  (?<host>[^\/:?#]+)
/x.freeze
```

Then reuse PATTERN.match(str) instead of Regexp.new per call. Profiling shows Regexp.new in a hot path taking ~5% CPU. Freezing constants prevents accidental mutation and helps JIT.

The Rack middleware adds response header normalization via downcasing and sorting headers on every response. This is not needed for most apps and is expensive. Provide a configuration to disable header sorting by default, and only enable for strict conformance modes. Consider using case-insensitive lookup structure instead of sorting arrays each time.

The streaming CSV parser yields each row as an Array, then our code converts to a Hash with headers per row. Can the library expose an option to yield a frozen Hash keyed to a shared frozen headers array? That would drop array->hash conversion per row and reduce allocations. Benchmarks with 1M rows suggest ~1.4x throughput improvement possible.

I’m seeing high GC time due to repeated creation of BigDecimal in the financial rounding routine. Can we provide a fixed-scale integer arithmetic mode to avoid BigDecimal unless necessary? For example, representing currency in cents internally, and only converting on I/O boundaries. Expose a configuration flag to avoid BigDecimal for performance-critical calculations.

We’re using your LRU cache and noticed it holds a Mutex per node, which is heavy. Can we refactor to a single striped lock or use a lock-free algorithm with RCU-like reads? Also, please expose cache stats (hit/miss/evictions) cheaply, to help us tune sizes. The current #stats builds strings and hashes on every call; make it lazy and optional.

The batch API client currently uses Net::HTTP without persistent connections. Under load, establishing new connections hurts latency. Can we add connection pooling (keep-alive) with per-host pools and request pipelining where supported? Provide backoff logic for 429/503 and a circuit breaker to avoid hammering. Bonus: an adapter for httpx to leverage multiplexing.

We’re hitting a lot of symbol GC churn with dynamic method names created via define_method in our DSL. Consider switching to define_singleton_method with precomputed symbols or using method_missing with a fast dispatch table and caching. The goal is to avoid creating a new Symbol for each dynamic attribute at runtime.

Our XML builder uses string concatenation in loops. Suggest using StringIO or a pre-sized String with capacity hint via String.new(capacity: n) (Ruby 3.2+) to minimize reallocations. Example:

```ruby
buf = String.new(capacity: 16_384)
# ... append
```

Provide a fallback for older Ruby versions.

I profiled a JSON endpoint and found that your symbolize_keys deep transformation is recursive and allocates many intermediate hashes. Could we implement a destructive in-place variant that reuses the existing Hash where safe? Provide a flag deep: false to only convert top-level keys. Please include benchmarks and ensure frozen input raises or is copied minimally.

We noticed high CPU when using the default YAML loader for configs. Switching to Psych YAML.safe_load with permitted classes defined sped things up a bit. Could we provide a precompiled schema or defaults, and maybe support a JSON parser fallback when the YAML is actually JSON? Many of our configs are JSON-like; detecting and routing to a faster parser would help.

In the CSV importer, validating headers uses regexes with catastrophic backtracking for malformed inputs. This can lock up the process on adversarial data. Replace the regex with a linear-time parser or add possessive quantifiers if we must keep regex. Include fuzz tests and a max length guard to keep parsing time bounded.

We’ve hit issues with String#split on large logs creating massive arrays. Please add a streaming line reader that yields slices using StringScanner or by scanning for newline indexes and yielding substrings via String#slice without dup. Ideally, callers can request a frozen copy or a view-like object. Provide a benchmark with 100MB logs.

In our GraphQL integration, response hashes get deep-copied before instrumentation. This is killing performance. Can we use immutable structures or structural sharing (e.g., Hamster/Immutable) to avoid full copies, or at least only copy modified branches? Add a config to opt out of copying in trusted environments.

We’re seeing hotspot in Base64 encoding where the library calls [string].pack repeatedly. Ruby has Base64.strict_encode64 which is C-optimized. Can we switch to that by default and only fall back to pack when line wrapping is requested? Also allow callers to pass a preallocated buffer.

Our log formatter uses Time.now for every line, causing syscalls and GC. Switch to a per-thread cached formatter with periodic time refresh (e.g., every second) to avoid strftime on each log. Something like:

```ruby
THREAD_TIME = ThreadLocalVar.new
# refresh once per second
```

Ensure correctness across timezone changes.

The HTTP client’s middleware stack is rebuilt per request. This allocates arrays and closures. Propose building the middleware chain once per client instance and freezing it. Example:

```ruby
@stack ||= build_stack.freeze
```

Then simply invoke @stack.call(env). Add thread-safety tests to ensure immutability.

We’re observing contention in the metrics aggregator due to a single global Hash updated with Mutex. Consider sharded counters (e.g., per-thread) and a periodic merge to a central map. Alternatively, use atomic integers and lock-free updates. Provide a benchmark with 32 threads incrementing counters to validate scalability.

The current implementation of our JSON encoder falls back to to_json for arbitrary objects, which allocates and is slow. Introduce a registry of encoders per class and a fast path for primitives. Also, avoid building a new String for commas/brackets: write directly to an IO-like buffer with preallocated separators. Include a microbenchmark comparing arrays of 100k ints.

When dealing with huge arrays, our map/filter chain creates many intermediate arrays. Can we return Enumerator::Lazy from filter/map helpers by default and only materialize if the caller asks? Provide an .to_a terminal operation. Update docs for backwards compatibility concerns.

The sanitizer uses CGI.escapeHTML which is fine but not the fastest. Consider using a native extension or replacing with a table-driven approach in pure Ruby that writes into a String buffer. Provide benchmark vs CGI.escapeHTML and ERB::Util.html_escape showing allocation counts and throughput.

We need to avoid repeated Dir.glob calls to load adapters on every request. Can we memoize the list at boot and support a reload! method for development? In production, this should be a frozen array and constant-time lookup. Provide a config flag eager_load: true to materialize at init.

Our retry middleware currently logs the full exception backtrace on every retry, which is expensive to build. Make backtrace capturing lazy or elide for known transient errors. Example:

```ruby
message = ex.message
backtrace = logger.debug? ? ex.backtrace : nil
```

Also, avoid String#% formatting unless log level requires it.

We found a quadratic algorithm in header normalization:

```ruby
normalized = headers.to_a.sort_by { |(k, _)| k.downcase }.to_h
```

Downcasing for every comparison is costly. Precompute downcased keys once and use a Schwartzian transform. Better, avoid sorting unless required by caller. Provide a fast path when input is already in canonical form.

On Ruby 3.3 with YJIT, splat args in hot methods kill performance. Example:

```ruby
def call(*args, **kwargs, &block)
  # hot path
end
```

Can we split into a fast path with fixed positional args and an infrequently used slow path? Also, avoid forwarding in internal calls when we know arity. Provide a benchmark comparing call overhead.

Our S3 uploader retries with exponential backoff but recalculates the signature on every retry, which is CPU heavy. Cache the canonical request and only recompute parts that change (date header). Also, reuse Net::HTTP connections or use aws-sigv4 gem if it’s faster. Provide a benchmark with throttled network and 5 retries.

The database adapter for Sequel uses typecasting that allocates String and Date objects for every row. Provide an option to return raw column values and let the caller cast selectively. This is especially useful in streaming queries where we drop most columns. Include examples and benchmarks.

Can we introduce a compiled path matcher for routing using a trie or a finite automaton instead of regex per route? For large route sets, regex matching is a bottleneck. Provide a build step that compiles routes at load time and a benchmark with 500 routes and 10k requests.

The following method is in a critical path and creates many temporary arrays via flatten/compact:

```ruby
def normalize_tags(tags)
  Array(tags).flatten.compact.map { |t| t.strip.downcase }.uniq
end
```

Proposed changes:
- Avoid flatten by iterating with a stack
- Skip compact by conditional checks
- Use a Set to dedup on the fly

Please add a benchmark comparing 10k tags with nested arrays and measure allocations via ObjectSpace::AllocationTracer.

We’ve seen repeated calls to Marshal.dump/load for caching structured objects. This is slow and version-fragile. Switch to MessagePack when available, else fallback. Provide a feature flag and ensure extension detection at load time. Add microbenchmarks and migration notes.

Stack trace and logs from our production incident suggest heavy GC and slow responses:

[info] request_id=abc124 duration=287ms allocations=11_992 gc_time=69ms

Flamegraph hotspots:
- String#split
- Hash#merge!
- ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument

Please refactor the event payload construction to avoid allocating when disabled, replace String#split with a streaming parser in the header parsing logic, and remove Hash#merge! in the hot path in favor of direct assignment. Provide before/after Benchmark.ips and allocation counts.

Repro for a CPU-bound loop in our library’s content hashing:

```ruby
require 'digest'

def content_digest(chunks)
  d = Digest::SHA256.new
  chunks.each { |c| d.update(c.to_s) }
  d.hexdigest
end

chunks = Array.new(100_000) { 'a' * 32 }
puts content_digest(chunks)
```

Issue: to_s allocates per chunk. Proposal: require IO/string inputs and forbid implicit conversion on hot path; or use String.try_convert and raise unless string. Also, allow passing an IO and use IO.copy_stream into an OpenSSL digest if available.

Error log shows frequent hash allocations during URL param encoding:

```
app[web.1]: param_encoder#encode allocations: 120_000 objects / request_id=xyz
```

Code:

```ruby
def encode(params)
  params.flat_map { |k, v| encode_pair(k, v) }.join('&')
end
```

Proposal: write directly to a String buffer and avoid flat_map/join. Use recursion with a shared buffer and pre-escaped tables. Add a benchmark with a nested hash of 1k keys.

When bulk importing 1M rows, the progress reporter fires an event per row, causing overhead. Add a sampling option (e.g., every N rows) and a monotonic clock-based throttle (e.g., min interval 200ms). Use Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) to avoid time travel issues.

The library’s default middleware captures caller locations via Kernel.caller on every request, which is expensive. Please make caller capturing opt-in and use Kernel.caller_locations(1, 1) only when needed. Provide a benchmark across 100k invocations.

We found that allocating exceptions for control flow in parse failures is heavy. Add a parse(str, raise: false) that returns [ok, value_or_error] to avoid constructing backtraces on common invalid inputs. Document and deprecate exception-heavy path in future major versions.

On Ruby 3.2, using Fiber.schedule in our async client yields good performance, but your code sometimes calls sleep and blocks. Make the scheduler-aware waits by using Thread.pass or Fiber-aware timers. Provide an adapter for async and falcon ecosystems and fall back to blocking when no scheduler.

Re: database batching. Our Upsert helper calls INSERT ... ON CONFLICT per row. We need a batch upsert builder that groups 1k rows per statement, uses prepared statements, and slices columns. Example API:


Benchmark: expect 10x throughput and fewer allocations.

Can we add ETag/Last-Modified headers on GET /notifications so the UI can cache and poll efficiently? The current behavior returns 200 on every poll and wastes bandwidth. Include strong ETags based on content hash and support If-None-Match.
The mobile client needs lighter payloads. Add a query param view=compact to trim nested fields and large blobs from /feed items. Document the field list in OpenAPI and ensure backward compatibility.

Improve error payload shape for upload failures. The UI needs a machine-readable code, a short display message, and an optional remediation URL. Standardize across 4xx and 5xx so the toast component can reuse.

For the settings page, please implement a feature flag endpoint that can return a structured list of UI experiments (name, description, enabled, rollout_percent). The UI consumes this list to toggle components. Ensure it’s safe to cache for 1 minute and include a signed checksum to detect changes.

The search results grid needs server-side sorting and stable, cursor-based pagination for smooth infinite scrolling. Add sort=created_at|name|relevance and direction=asc|desc, and return a next_cursor token. Ensure stable ordering under concurrent inserts and document cursor expiry behavior.

Add content negotiation so the admin console can request application/vnd.example.item+json;v=2. We need schema evolution: deprecate field legacy_label and add display_label with fallback. Include deprecation warnings in a custom response header so the UI can surface warnings in dev builds.

Our UI accessibility audits are failing due to missing alt text on images. Add alt_text and aria_label fields to /assets responses. If we don’t have author-provided text, return a smart default such as the filename (without extension) truncated to 80 chars.

Please implement server-sent events (SSE) at /events/stream for live status updates. The UI will subscribe and show progress bars. We need reconnection support with Last-Event-ID, heartbeat every 15s, and backpressure-safe write buffering.

Add an endpoint to get aggregated counts used for UI badges (unread notifications, pending tasks, failed jobs). The dashboard currently makes 3+ calls. Return a single JSON with counts and a last_updated timestamp, cacheable for 5s.

We need a deterministic color assignment service for user avatars in the UI. Add GET /ui/color-hash?seed=<string> returning a hex color from a curated palette, with WCAG AA contrast guidelines when paired with white text. Include palette version in response for cache-busting.

Update the OpenAPI descriptions and examples to include UI-focused details: max lengths, placeholder examples, and example error payloads for form fields. The docs power our Form Builder and currently render poorly due to missing examples.
